item.title: V-Representability Beyond Singular Times in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: The Hubbard Dimer Case
item.description: arXiv:2610.33837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the global $V$-representability problem in time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for the two-particle Hubbard dimer model in the spin-singlet sector. In particular, we investigate whether the time-dependent density of the interacting system obtained for a given one-body external potential $u$ (the tunable control variable) can be reproduced by a non-interacting Kohn--Sham system beyond the singular times at which the usual inversion formulas break down. We deal with both the conventional formulation of TDDFT based on some time-dependent variational principle and the recently introduced geometric formulation of TDDFT (Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 (2026) 256401, Phys. Rev. A 113 (2026) 062222). For both principles, we prove global-in-time $V$-representability, show that singular times induce non-uniqueness of the time-dependent effective potential, and classify the set of solutions.
item.dc:creator: \'Eric Canc\`es, Th\'eo Duez

item.title: On the uniqueness of translation-invariant ground states of the $S=1$ Heisenberg and $J$--$D$ antiferromagnetic chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.34330v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using the analytic machinery and numerical inputs of OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we prove uniqueness of the translation-invariant ground state of the infinite $S=1$ Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain and of the $J$-$D$ model for sufficiently small $|D|$. Uniqueness is among all translation-invariant ground states in the operator-algebraic sense, without assuming a gap or spin-rotation symmetry for a competing state. The proof combines concentration of the spatial transfer spectrum, an exponentially small low-temperature free-energy correction, and a Golden--Thompson comparison for separated local observables. The unique translation-invariant state is pure, locally unique and gapped, and continuous in $D$. The ground states of even periodic chains and odd open chains with equal positive endpoint fields converge to this state along their full sequences, uniformly in $D$, with a stretched-exponential local rate. Every choice of ground states of open chains without endpoint magnetic fields has the same local limit. These conclusions do not establish uniqueness among arbitrary nontranslation-invariant ground states of the infinite chain. The author formulated the problems and proposed the core strategies. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to developing the proofs and preparing the manuscript.
item.dc:creator: Hal Tasaki

item.title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
item.description: arXiv:2610.34470v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Bellomia, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera, Massimo Capone, Adriano Amaricci

item.title: Rigorous Lower Bounds for Atomic and Ionic Ground-State Energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.34480v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a new iterative method for computing rigorous lower bounds for the ground-state energies of all atoms and ions. The accuracy of the resulting bounds depends on two ingredients: the quality of the initial energy estimate and the quality of the used upper bound for the maximum number of bound electrons, $N_c(Z)$, as a function of the nuclear charge $Z>0$. In particular, this new method allows us to establish the explicit lower bound $E(N,Z) \geq -0.8710\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for the ground-state energy $E(N,Z)$ of the atom/ion with $N \in \mathbb{N}$ electrons and nuclear charge $Z \in (0,N]$, thereby considerably improving the best known constant $A=(3/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.1447$ in the estimate $E(N,Z) \geq -A\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for $0 < Z \leq N$ and coming much closer to the best possible constant given by the Thomas-Fermi asymptotics $\lim_{N \to \infty} |E(N,N)|N^{-7/3}= -E_{\text{TF}}(1)\approx 0.7687$ derived in Adv. Math., 23(1) by Lieb and Simon. To demonstrate the potential and the limits of our method, we also compute explicit lower bounds for the ground-state energies $E(N,N)$ of all atoms with $2 \leq N \leq 86$ and we compare them with the bounds obtained in J. Chem. Phys., 62(8) by Hertel, Lieb, Thirring and the bounds obtained by Seco in his dissertation. Finally, we also provide a uniqueness result for the expectation values of the kinetic, potential and interaction energies on the ground-state space.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hofacker

item.title: Higher Order OTOCs in Chaotic Quantum Maps: Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances and Asymptotic Freeness
item.description: arXiv:2610.34615v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) measure the scrambling of information and are a powerful diagnostic of chaos. In chaotic quantum systems with a classical analog, their relaxation towards equilibrium is dictated by the classical Ruelle--Pollicott resonances. We investigate higher-order OTOCs in quantum maps, prototypical one-body systems with a classical limit showing all the essential features of chaotic dynamics. We demonstrate numerically that in the intermediate-time regime they decay exponentially at a rate that depends only on the parity of the order: odd-order OTOCs decay at the same rate as classical correlations, given by the leading Ruelle--Pollicott resonance, and even-order ones at twice that rate. Both are far slower than the naive expectation, under which the rate would grow in proportion to the order. We then mimic the effect of an environment by defining a coarse-grained superoperator whose effect is to introduce decoherence into the system, and find that the expected proportionality between rate and order is thereby restored. Finally, we show that at long times each higher-order OTOC becomes dominated by a single free cumulant, whose saturation value falls off inversely with the dimension of the Hilbert space, signalling the emergence of asymptotic freeness and highlighting the relevance of free probability theory as a framework for the study of quantum chaos.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\'as G\'omez Brucks, Ignacio Garc\'ia-Mata, Diego A. Wisniacki

item.title: Helicity-Selective Electron-Phonon Coupling Between $PT$-Partner States in $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.34830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rotational symmetry ($C_n$) constrains chiral phonons, but how other symmetries affect their interactions remains largely unexplored. We perform a theoretical and computational study of chiral phonon coupling to parity-time ($PT$)-degenerate electron doublets in $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$. Although $PT$ suppresses phonon singlet chirality, chiral phonon doublets can helically interact with $PT$-partner electronic states via a mechanism similar to pseudospin. Selection rules are then analyzed with the interplay of $PT$ and $C_3$. Our computational results of $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$ suggest chiral phonons may be used to resolve intravalley electronic states in $PT$ systems.
item.dc:creator: Fred Sun, Jia-An Yan

item.title: Large Language Models for Quantum Code Translation: An Exploratory Study
item.description: arXiv:2610.34841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum software development is challenged by quantum-mechanical semantics and fragmented software development kits (SDKs), which complicate cross-SDK code translation and execution. In this paper, we propose an LLM-based approach for translating executable programs between high-level quantum SDKs. We develop a quantum-aware translation workflow whose prompt design and validation reflect quantum semantics and accommodate the version evolution of quantum ecosystems. We conduct a preliminary evaluation of 4 LLM configurations on 43 tasks, translating Qiskit programs to PennyLane and Q#. LLMs achieve a zero-shot Pass@1 of up to 72.33%, while one-shot prompting further improves the translation effectiveness. These results suggest potential for quantum code translation by LLMs.
item.dc:creator: Xiyuan Li, Yuechen Li, Jianjun Zhao

item.title: Photometric Redshift Estimation with Hybrid Quantum Neural Network
item.description: arXiv:2610.35196v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A Hybrid Quantum Neural Network (HQNN) is applied to recover the photometric redshift of a galaxy dataset built using data from two astronomical surveys, the Kilo-Degree Survey (KIDS) and the VISTA Kilo-Degree Infrared Galaxy (VIKING), which provide data with coverage from the optical to the near-infrared electromagnetic spectrum. The results are then compared with those obtained by a classical neural network. We see that HQNN consistently recovers the reference photometric redshift with a high statistical fidelity. Furthermore, both the $R^2$ and the MSE found by the HQNN are consistently better than those found by the classical counterpart (albeit consistent in the error range), proving the worth of further investigating these novel technologies for this particular astrophysical application.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Sarracino, Vincenzo Fabrizio Cardone, Irene Graziotti, Crescenzo Tortora, Roberto Scaramella, Andrea Bulgarelli, Carlo Burigana, Farida Farsian, Massimo Meneghetti, Giuseppe Murante, Niccol\`o Parmiggiani, Alessandro Rizzo, Francesco Schillir\`o, Vincenzo Testa, Tiziana Trombetti, Fabio Roberto Vitello

item.title: Bargmann-invariant witness of the graviton commutator
item.description: arXiv:2610.35253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We identify the phase of a Bargmann invariant of two matter-wave interferometers as a quantum gravity signature that cannot be reproduced by any branchwise-definite classical gravitational field. For matter coupled linearly to linearized gravity, the interferometric coherence factorizes exactly into a conservative Newtonian phase, the characteristic functional of the graviton state, and a commutator phase. For Wigner-positive graviton states, the first two are classically reproducible; therefore, decoherence alone cannot certify that gravity is quantized. The Bargmann phase isolates the commutator, which is independent of the graviton state and of all Newtonian interactions and is bounded by which-path decoherence. For gravity, this radiation-reaction effect is sixty orders of magnitude below experimental reach, but trapped-ion analogs can test it at order unity.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Matsui

item.title: Measurement-dependent reduction of open dynamics in the quantum phase estimation algorithm: the visible subspace and the damped Fej\'er kernel
item.description: arXiv:2610.35332v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the quantum phase estimation (QPE) algorithm we study the minimal space of observables that is sufficient to predict the entire output distribution under open dynamics of the counting register. Building on the general Krylov theory of reduction, we compute the structure of this space explicitly for the full Fourier measurement. The outcome probabilities are determined by cyclic sums of the state matrix. If the adjoint generator is diagonal on the matrix units, the spectral classes inside the residue classes of the index difference modulo the register dimension $M$ give a constructive basis, an exact dimension formula, and attainable bounds: the dimension of the visible space lies between $M$ and $M^2-M+1$. The class includes independent qubit dephasing, and an analytically solvable reference model of Gorini--Kossakowski--Lindblad--Sudarshan (GKLS) type yields a damped Fej\'er kernel; two random-unitary channels with the same Ramsey contrast show that higher harmonics are distinguishable in the QPE distribution. For approximate reduction we use a finite-time Gramian and an a posteriori residual estimate, with a quadratic error order for a reducing unperturbed subspace and a compatible initial state. Numerical calculations check the consistency of the representations and the behaviour of the error under non-Toeplitz perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Marina O. Gordeichuk, Oleg M. Kiselev

item.title: Compositional Operational Rank, Smooth Realizability, and Dimensional Reduction
item.description: arXiv:2610.35764v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Higher-dimensional theories distinguish the dimensionality of a microscopic description from the number of directions accessible to a physical observer. Relating these notions requires not only dimensional reduction, but also a consistent preservation of operational independence across different levels of description. We establish sufficient conditions under which a compositional operational rank is preserved first as the dimension of a smooth integral leaf and then as an observable Fisher-information rank. The key requirement is closure-faithfulness: the smooth realization must preserve the dependency relations of the operational closure, rather than merely its total rank. Together with real representability, constant rank, involutivity, and observer/scale compatibility, this yields a local integral leaf whose dimension equals the operational rank. A further primary-identification condition is required at the measurement level. If an independently specified observer image coincides locally with the primary integral distribution and the admissible protocols provide local resolution, finite labeled-mixture closure, and locally constant outcome support, then the same rank can be realized by a finite composite Fisher-information protocol. The construction holds for arbitrary finite rank. At r = 4 it provides a conditional operational criterion for dimensional reduction in higher-dimensional theories: a viable reduction must preserve the relevant operational dependency structure, not merely produce four effective coordinates. Quantum-hardware negative controls further show that the same restricted Fisher rank can conceal different larger ranks under a broader pre-specified measurement protocol. The framework therefore constrains the operational outcome of dimensional reduction without imposing a universal four-dimensional bound on microscopic state spaces.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay D. Tulupov, Alexander M. Tishin

item.title: Growth Phase Map of {\alpha} and \b{eta} Tantalum as a Function of Growth Temperature and Oxygen Partial Pressure
item.description: arXiv:2610.35768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tantalum thin films are used in low-loss superconducting quantum circuits, yet the growth conditions governing selection of $\alpha$-Ta(110), $\alpha$-Ta(111), and metastable $\beta$-Ta on c-plane sapphire remain uncertain. We deposited 100 nm Ta films by dc magnetron sputtering on Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) at 300-900 $^\circ$C while varying the O$_2$ partial pressure from a $5.5\times10^{-11}$ Torr ultrahigh-vacuum baseline to $2.23\times10^{-4}$ Torr. Absorption-corrected X-ray diffraction texture coefficients were used to construct a ternary phase-orientation growth map in terms of temperature and the oxygen-to-Ta impingement flux ratio ($2\Phi_{O_2}/\Phi_{Ta}\leq4.8\times10^{-6}$ to 19). Without added oxygen, $\alpha$-Ta(110) dominated at every temperature. At an O$_2$ pressure of only $2.5\times10^{-9}$ Torr ($2\Phi_{O_2}/\Phi_{Ta}=2.2\times10^{-4}$), $\alpha$-Ta(111) accounted for 98-99% of the normalized texture weight from 300 to 700 $^\circ$C, decreasing to 65% at 900 $^\circ$C. Substantial $\beta$-Ta formed only at the highest oxygen dose, dominating at 300 $^\circ$C and disappearing at 900 $^\circ$C. The apparent $\beta$(001)/$\alpha$(110) selection energy of $1.07\pm0.16$ eV is comparable to the activation energy for oxygen diffusion in Ta, consistent with oxygen transport influencing phase selection. Oxygen also produced orientation-dependent changes in crystallite size and microstrain. These findings establish oxygen-controlled processing windows for phase- and orientation-selective growth of Ta films for superconducting devices.
item.dc:creator: Marius O. Eji, Tyler J. Kirkpatrick, Ty J. Cawein, Joseph P. Corbett

item.title: How Retrocausality Helps
item.description: arXiv:1706.02290v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It has become increasingly apparent that a number of perplexing issues associated with the interpretation of quantum mechanics are more easily resolved once the notion of retrocausality is introduced. The aim here is to list and discuss various examples where a clear explanation has become available via this approach. In so doing, the intention is to highlight that this direction of research deserves more attention than it presently receives.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: AIP Conference Proceedings - Quantum Retrocausation III, pp. 1-5 (2016)
item.dc:creator: Roderick Sutherland

item.title: A semi-classical analysis of the coupling strength $\gamma$ between motional quantum states of spatially distant trapped ions interacting via a conducting wire
item.description: arXiv:2111.14957v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Interfacing ion qubits in separate traps is among the challenges towards scaling up trapped ion quantum computing. This theoretical study focuses on using a conducting wire to couple the motional quantum states of ions in separate planar traps. The approach of interfacing ion traps provides an alternative to coupling distant qubits with lasers or via ion shuttling. We develop a detailed model for the coupling strength $\gamma$, which in turn allows us to calculate the time required to exchange motional quantum states between two ions, $t_{\mathrm{ex.}}$. To maximize the coupling strength $\gamma$, a rule of thumb is developed to relate the distance $d_{\mathrm{eq.}}$ between a trapped ion and a nearby pickup disk, to the optimal radius $r_{\mathrm{opt.}}$ of the disk, $d_{\mathrm{eq.}} / \sqrt{2} \le r_{\mathrm{opt.}} \le d_{\mathrm{eq.}}$. We include a coefficient $\zeta$ which describes three self-capacitances connected in series, relating the capacitances of each part of the coupling system, which corrects an oversight common to several previous works. Our analytical model for the coupling strength is then compared with other existing analytical models in the literature. This requires a standardization of the coupling systems and mapping them to a common set of parameter values. Similarities, differences and limitations of the various models are discussed. This study's focus on the coupling strength $\gamma$ and $t_{\mathrm{ex.}}$ provides a foundational pillar for exchanging quantum information between trapped ions via a wire. In addition, many insights are general and apply broadly to hybrid systems interfacing trapped ions with nearby conductors.
item.dc:creator: N. Van Horne, M. Mukherjee

item.title: Generalized coherent states and uncertainty relations in $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric position dependent mass systems
item.description: arXiv:2208.10336v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate a class of $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric quantum systems with position-dependent effective mass (PDEM). We factorize the PDEM Hamiltonian using a pair of first order differential operators. The resulting commutation relation introduces the notion of a position-dependent effective Planck parameter, which reduces to Planck's constant in the conventional Hermitian quantum system with constant mass. These factorization operators define a deformed phase space, within which we construct generalized coherent states to first order in the $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetry parameter. We then revisit the Heisenberg uncertainty principle for this state and demonstrate that the deformed position and momentum operators satisfy the corresponding uncertainty relation in the $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric PDEM framework. Finally, we present explicit computational results for a toy-model oscillator with position-dependent effective mass in a $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric setting. In the conclusions section, we outline a gedankenexperiment for experimental determination of $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric parameter.
item.dc:creator: Pinaki Patra

item.title: A general quantum circuit framework for Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios: logically and causally consistent reasoning without absolute measurement events
item.description: arXiv:2209.09281v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios (EWFSs) model agents themselves as unitarily evolving quantum systems, going beyond the standard use of quantum theory where agents are treated classically. Several no-go results suggest deep challenges in this setting: Frauchiger and Renner (FR) argued that quantum agents reasoning using quantum theory would arrive at logical paradoxes, while the Local-Friendliness theorem raises difficulties for maintaining objective notions of measurement events and causal reasoning in EWFSs. This prompts a key question: can the ability to make and test scientific predictions and reason consistently still be maintained if quantum theory applies universally, even to agents and their memories? We answer this positively by developing a general quantum circuit framework for EWFSs without assuming absolute measurement outcomes. We formalize Heisenberg cuts in terms of distinct choices of channels in the circuit, labelled by "settings", and show that FR-type paradoxes are fully resolved by making explicit the conditioning on these channels/settings. We provide concrete reasoning rules for quantum agents that ensure logical, probabilistic and causal consistency. Our framework captures all perspectives in an EWFS within a single causal structure while allowing events to be fundamentally subjective, and we show how objective events and predictions nevertheless emerge in current real-world quantum experiments. Thus, we demonstrate a relational yet operational framework that overcomes key challenges in EWFSs without altering the Born rule, unitarity, or classical logic and probability for outcomes. This establishes a formal platform to analyze and compare different EWFS arguments and extend quantum information methods consistently into the Wigner's Friend domain.
item.dc:creator: V. Vilasini, Mischa P. Woods

item.title: Compressing multivariate functions with tree tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2410.03572v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tensor networks are a compressed format for multi-dimensional data. One dimensional tensor networks -- often referred to as tensor trains (TT) or matrix product states (MPS) -- are increasingly being used as a numerical ansatz for continuum functions by ``quantizing'' the inputs into discrete binary digits. Here we demonstrate the power of more general tree tensor networks (TTNs) for this purpose. We provide direct constructions of a number of elementary functions as generic tree tensor networks and interpolative constructions for more complicated functions via a generalization of the tensor cross interpolation algorithm. For a range of multi-dimensional functions we show how more structured tree tensor networks offer a significantly more efficient ansatz than the commonly used tensor train. Finally, we demonstrate how the methods introduced in this work can be used to realize a TTN-based solver for multi-dimensional, non-linear Fredholm equations.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Tindall, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Ryan Levy

item.title: Conditional Motional Squeezing of an Optomechanical Oscillator Approaching the Quantum Regime
item.description: arXiv:2410.09208v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Squeezed mechanical states are a highly coveted resource for quantum-enhanced sensing and serve as a compelling platform for probing the interplay between gravity and quantum mechanics. It has been predicted that a mechanical oscillator can be prepared into a quantum squeezed state if the applied measurement rate is fast relative to its mechanical resonance frequency. However, the experimental feasibility of this protocol has remained uncertain because of the difficulty in achieving low-frequency oscillators with sufficiently strong read-out. Here, we demonstrate that a careful selection of parameters in an optomechanical system, combined with optimal filtering techniques, enables the preparation of a 50 ng GaAs cantilever in a conditional classical squeezed state, achieving a minimum uncertainty of just 1.07 plus/minus 0.04 times the zero-point fluctuation level. This minimum variance is 3 orders of magnitude smaller than what has been achieved in previous experiments using the same protocol. Although we do not fully achieve the quantum squeezed regime, our demonstration provides definitive evidence that a measurement-based protocol is a practical and effective approach for the real-time preparation of macroscopic oscillators in quantum squeezed states.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin B. Lane, Junxin Chen, Ronald E. Pagano, Scott Aronson, Garrett D. Cole, Xinghui Yin, Thomas R. Corbitt, Nergis Mavalvala

item.title: Higher-order exceptional points in a non-reciprocal waveguide beam splitter
item.description: arXiv:2503.21445v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-Hermitian systems have attracted significant interest because of their intriguing properties, including exceptional points (EPs), where eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenstates coalesce. In particular, quantum systems with EPs exhibit an enhanced sensitivity to external perturbations, which increases with the order of the EP. Therefore, higher-order EPs hold significant potential for advanced sensing applications, but they are challenging to achieve due to stringent symmetry requirements. In this work, we study the dynamics of a generalized lossy waveguide beam splitter with asymmetric coupling by introducing non-reciprocity as a tunable parameter to achieve higher-order EPs even without dissipation. Moreover, we analyze the evolution of NOON-states under activated non-reciprocity, highlighting its impact on quantum systems. Our results open new pathways for realizing higher-order EPs in non-reciprocal open quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Ghaemi-Dizicheh, Shahram Dehdashti, Andreas Hanke, Ahmed Touhami, Janis N\"otzel

item.title: Simon's Period Finding on a Quantum Annealer
item.description: arXiv:2504.10771v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dating to 1994, Simon's period-finding algorithm is among the earliest and most fragile of quantum algorithms. The algorithm's fragility arises from the requirement that, to solve an n qubit problem, one must fault-tolerantly sample O(n) linearly independent values from a solution space. In this paper, we study an adiabatic implementation of Simon's algorithm that requires a constant number of successful samples regardless of problem size. We implement this algorithm on D-Wave hardware and solve problems with up to 298 qubits. We compare the runtime of classical algorithms to the D-Wave solution to analyze any potential advantage.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Quantum Computing and Engineering (QCE) 1, 190 (2025)
item.dc:creator: Reece Robertson, Emery Doucet, Zakaria Mzaouali, Krzysztof Domino, Bart{\l}omiej Gardas, Sebastian Deffner

item.title: Intrinsic Hamiltonian of Mean Force and Strong-Coupling Quantum Thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2506.02888v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a universal thermodynamic framework for quantum systems strongly coupled to thermal reservoirs, identifying the class of initial conditions required for consistent thermodynamic behavior. Unlike other approaches, our framework provides a unified description of both thermodynamic processes and thermostatic properties, while preserving the same gauge freedoms as in the standard weak-coupling regime and retaining the von Neumann expression for the thermodynamic entropy. Furthermore, the formulation is entirely in terms of the system's reduced state, relying only on variables accessible through local microscopic control. It is therefore directly connected to experimentally accessible quantities, making it possible to address operational questions concerning the controlled system-such as determining the minimum work required to drive it between two prescribed states in the presence of a strongly coupled reservoir. We validate our approach using a paradigmatic model of a structured bosonic reservoir.
item.dc:creator: Ignacio Gonz\'alez, Sagnik Chakraborty, \'Angel Rivas

item.title: Quantum Counting in the Rydberg Blockade
item.description: arXiv:2506.19298v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a quantum algorithm for approximately counting the number of solutions to planar 2-satisfiability (2SAT) formulas natively on neutral-atom quantum computers (NAQC). Our algorithm maps Boolean variables to atomic registers arranged in space according to a given formula, so that 2SAT constraints are enforced via the Rydberg blockade between neighboring atoms. A quench of an initial computational basis state then produces a superposition of all solutions after sufficiently long evolution. For almost uniform superpositions, a polynomial number of measurements is enough to estimate the solution count up to any constant multiplicative factor via sampling-based counting. Numerical simulations show that the protocol leads to almost uniform solution sampling in 1D and 2D grids and produces accurate counts for small random 2SAT instances on punctured grids. We implement our algorithm on Pasqal's Orion Alpha NAQC and demonstrate approximate counts within small multiplicative factors of the exact count for a planar grid instance with 81 atoms.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Gibson, Victor Drouin-Touchette, Stefanos Kourtis

item.title: Fully Parallelized BP Decoding for Quantum LDPC Codes Can Outperform BP-OSD
item.description: arXiv:2507.00254v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work presents a hardware-efficient and fully parallelizable decoder for quantum LDPC codes that leverages belief propagation (BP) with a speculative post-processing strategy inspired by classical Chase decoding algorithm. By monitoring bit-level oscillation patterns during BP, our method identifies unreliable bits and generates multiple candidate vectors to selectively flip syndromes. Each modified syndrome is then decoded independently using short-depth BP, a process we refer to as BP-SF (syndrome flip). This design eliminates the need for costly Gaussian elimination used in the current BP-OSD approaches. Our implementation achieves logical error rates comparable to or better than BP-OSD while offering significantly lower latency due to its high degree of parallelism for a variety of bivariate bicycle codes. Evaluation on the $[[144,12,12]]$ bivariate bicycle code shows that the proposed decoder reduces average latency to approximately 70% of BP-OSD. When post-processing is parallelized the average latency is reduced to 55% compared to the single process implementation, with the maximum latency reaching as low as 18%. These advantages make it particularly well-suited for real-time and resource-constrained quantum error correction systems.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 2026 IEEE International Symposium on High Performance Computer Architecture (HPCA), pp. 1-14, 2026
item.dc:creator: Ming Wang, Ang Li, Frank Mueller

item.title: One-sided Witnesses for the Quantumness of Gravitational Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2507.15588v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum information concepts and quantum technologies have opened the prospect of probing the quantum nature of gravity in table-top experiments. Most proposals rely on detecting gravitationally mediated entanglement, which requires measurements on both interacting systems. Here we propose an alternative test based on witnessing quantum memory effects in the dynamics of a single system. We show how the quantum memory concept allows the non-classicality of the interaction between two systems to be certified through local measurements on only one of them. We then develop a novel quantum memory witness, making the approach applicable to gravitationally coupled harmonic oscillators. This witness requires no assumptions about the dynamics, such as Gaussianity. Our results show that the quantumness of gravitational dynamics can be certified with access to only one subsystem, opening the door to asymmetric implementations that can offer conceptual and experimental advantages to probing the quantum nature of the gravitational interaction.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Beyer, M. S. Kim, Igor Pikovski

item.title: Anyonic membranes and Pontryagin statistics
item.description: arXiv:2509.14314v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Anyons, unique to two spatial dimensions, underlie extraordinary phenomena such as the fractional quantum Hall effect, but their generalization to higher dimensions has remained elusive. The topology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces constrains the loop statistics to be only bosonic or fermionic in any dimension. In this work, we introduce the novel anyonic statistics for membrane excitations in four dimensions. Analogous to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-particle exhibiting $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(2,N)}$ anyonic statistics in two dimensions, we show that the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-membrane possesses $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(3,N)}$ anyonic statistics in four dimensions. Given unitary volume operators that create membrane excitations on the boundary, we propose an explicit 56-step unitary sequence that detects the membrane statistics. We further analyze the boundary theory of $(5{+}1)$D 1-form $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry-protected topological phases and demonstrate that their domain walls realize all possible anyonic membrane statistics. We then show that the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ subgroup persists in all higher dimensions. In addition to the standard fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2$ membrane statistics arising from Stiefel-Whitney classes, membranes also exhibit $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics associated with Pontryagin classes. We explicitly verify that the 56-step process detects the nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics in 5, 6, and 7 spatial dimensions. Moreover, in 7 and higher dimensions, the statistics of membrane excitations stabilize to $\mathbb{Z}_{2} \times \mathbb{Z}_{3}$, with the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ sector consistently captured by this process.
item.dc:creator: Yitao Feng, Hanyu Xue, Yuyang Li, Meng Cheng, Ryohei Kobayashi, Po-Shen Hsin, Yu-An Chen

item.title: Universal two-excitation scattering in two-dimensional subwavelength atomic arrays
item.description: arXiv:2509.17085v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Subwavelength atomic arrays are a leading platform for engineering strong light-matter interactions, presenting exciting opportunities for quantum science. However, a full understanding of their multi-excitation dynamics remains a significant challenge. In this Letter, we uncover a remarkable universal phenomenon that emerges in these arrays. Using scattering theory to analyze two-excitation interactions, we reveal a profound simplification near critical points of the collective atomic excitation band structure, determined solely from single-excitation properties. At these critical points, which emerge as band edges and saddle points (Van Hove singularities) in the two-excitation phase space, scattering becomes universal and the full two-excitation scattering matrix decomposes into a block-diagonal form. Remarkably, all scattering processes involving the photon field are completely suppressed, resulting in the perfect isolation of a unitary, nonlinear interaction channel between collective dark spin waves. Our findings provide exact analytical insights into few-body nonlinearities and establish a universal framework for analyzing complex scattering phenomena in ordered atomic systems.
item.dc:creator: Yidan Wang, Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, Valentin Walther, Susanne F. Yelin

item.title: Proofs of Quantum Memory
item.description: arXiv:2510.04159v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new concept, proofs of quantum memory (PoQM). A PoQM is an interactive protocol between a classical verifier and a quantum prover over a classical channel where the verifier can verify that the prover has possessed a specified number of qubits for a specified period of time. PoQM generalize proofs of quantumness (PoQ) [Brakerski, Christiano, Mahadev, Vazirani, and Vidick, JACM 2021] where a classical verifier can verify that the prover is not classical. Our contributions are summarized as follows: We introduce PoQM. We also introduce a variant of PoQM, which we call inefficient-verifier PoQM (IV-PoQM), where the verifier's final computation to make the decision is not necessarily efficient. We construct PoQM based on the hardness of LWE. Specifically, we give two constructions of PoQM. The first one is of two-round and has negligible soundness error under the subexponential-hardness of LWE. The second one is of polynomial-round and has inverse-polynomial soundness error under the polynomial-hardness of LWE. We show that IV-PoQM imply one-way puzzles. Moreover, we show that a certain restricted version of PoQM implies quantum computation classical communication key exchange, which suggests the difficulty of black-box constructing PoQM from one-way functions. We show that constant-round PoQ imply PoQM or single-round PoQ (with a quantum verifier). Single-round PoQ are ``trivial'' PoQ in the sense that the verifier asks the prover to solve a classical problem which is quantumly easy but classically hard. The result therefore demonstrates that PoQM capture ``genuinely-interactive'' PoQ. We show that if constant-round IV-PoQ that are black-box constructed from quantumly-secure falsifiable assumptions exist then IV-PoQM exist. This result implies that IV-PoQM can be constructed from quantumly-secure constant-round statistically-hiding commitments.
item.dc:creator: Minki Hhan, Tomoyuki Morimae, Yasuaki Okinaka, Takashi Yamakawa

item.title: Complementarity in quantum and general information theories
item.description: arXiv:2510.10800v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an operational definition of complementarity, pinning down the concept originally introduced by Bohr. Two properties of a system are considered complementary if the definiteness of their values conflicts. We show that, within quantum theory, this notion is equivalent to the incompatibility of operations, that is, their inability to be performed simultaneously. We further show that for a generic information theory, the instruments associated with complementary properties are incompatible.
item.dc:creator: Davide Rolino, Paolo Perinotti, Alessandro Tosini

item.title: Exact and approximate conditions of tabletop reversibility: when is Petz recovery cost-free?
item.description: arXiv:2510.26895v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Channels $\mathcal{N}$ that describe open quantum dynamics are inherently irreversible: it is impossible to undo their effect completely, but one can study partial recovery of the information. The Petz recovery map $\hat{\mathcal{N}}_{\gamma}^{(\texttt{P})}$ is a systematic construction that depends only on $\mathcal{N}$ and on a reference state $\gamma$, which will be recovered exactly. If the real input state was different from $\gamma$, the recovery is partial, with a guarantee of near-optimality. Generically, an implementation of the Petz recovery map would look very different from the implementation of the channel. It is natural to study under which conditions the two maps require similar or even identical resources. The noisy forward channel $\mathcal{N}$ is called ``tabletop time-reversible'' for a given $\gamma$ when the corresponding Petz recovery map is realizable in such a way. First, we study the exact tabletop reversibility (TTR) conditions. We show in particular that a time-sensitive control of an ancilla system is needed. Second, we present the approximate TTR conditions, which do not require such a time-sensitive control. Third, we derive Lindbladian TTR conditions under a random-time collision model.
item.dc:creator: Minjeong Song, Hyukjoon Kwon, Valerio Scarani

item.title: Distributed quantum approximate counting algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2511.04945v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we propose a distributed quantum algorithm for solving counting problem using Grover operator and a classical post-processing procedure. We apply the proposed algorithm to estimate inner products and Hamming distances. Simulations are conducted on the Qisikit platform, further demonstrating the effectiveness of our algorithm and its suitability for the NISQ era. Compared to existing counting algorithms, the proposed algorithm has advantages in terms of the number of qubits, circuit depth, and the number of quantum gates.
item.dc:creator: Huaijing Huang, Daowen Qiu

item.title: Nonclassicality of a Macroscopic Qubit-Ensemble via Parity Measurement Induced Disturbance
item.description: arXiv:2511.15880v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an experimental scheme to test the nonclassicality of a macroscopic ensemble of qubits, through the violation of the classical notion of macrorealism (MR) via the fundamental measurement-induced disturbance of quantum systems. An electromagnetic resonator is used to probe the parity of the qubit-ensemble. The action of sequential measurements allows the nonclassicality of whole ensemble to manifest itself, in the ideal case, irrespective of its size. This enables to probe the macroscopic limits of quantum mechanics as the qubit-ensemble is, effectively, a single large spin of many $\hbar$ units. Even as $\hbar \rightarrow 0$ in comparison to the total angular momentum of the ensemble, a constant amount of violation of MR is found in the noiseless case. However, environmental decoherence and inhomogeneity of qubit-electromagnetic field couplings precipitate the quantum-to-classical transition. This illustrates that Bohr's correspondence principle is not fundamental, but a consequence of practical limitations. We outline an implementation with a variety of qubits (superconducting qubits, spins in semiconductors, and Rydberg atoms) coupled to a coplanar waveguide resonator, and -- via the corresponding noise analysis -- find that violation of MR is detectable up to $100$ qubits via current technology.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Braccini, Debarshi Das, Ben Zindorf, Stephen D. Hogan, John J. L. Morton, Sougato Bose

item.title: Quantum measurement retrodiction and entropic uncertainty relations
item.description: arXiv:2511.20281v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study quantum measurement retrodiction using the principle of minimum change. For quantum-to-classical measurement channels, we show that all standard quantum divergences select the same retrodictive update, yielding a unique and divergence-independent quantum Bayesian inverse for any POVM and prior state. Using this update, we construct a symmetric joint distribution for pairs of POVMs and introduce the mutual retrodictability, for which we also derive a general upper bound that depends only on the prior state and holds for all measurements. This structure leads to two retrodictive entropic uncertainty relations, expressed directly in terms of the prior state and the POVMs, but valid independently of the retrodictive framework and fully compatible with the conventional operational interpretation of entropic uncertainty relations. Finally, we benchmark these relations numerically and find that they provide consistently tighter bounds than existing entropic uncertainty relations over broad classes of measurements and states.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxi Kuang, Kensei Torii, Francesco Buscemi

item.title: Quantum Sensing using Geometrical Phase in Qubit-Oscillator Systems
item.description: arXiv:2511.21983v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a quantum sensing protocol for coupled qubit-oscillator systems that surpasses the standard quantum limit (SQL) by exploiting a geometrical phase. The signal is encoded in the geometrical phase that is proportional to the area enclosed in oscillator phase space. This area is amplified through squeezing, enabling sensitivities beyond the SQL. Our method is independent of oscillator's initial state, amenable to sensing with high-temperature or logical error-corrected states. The protocol shows robustness to qubit Markovian noise and preserves its state-independence, underscoring its practicality for next-generation quantum metrology. We demonstrate application to force sensing beyond the SQL in longitudinally coupled systems, and to high-precision measurements of couplings and pulse calibration surpassing SQL in dispersively coupled circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) architectures.
item.dc:creator: Nishchay Suri, Zhihui Wang, Tanay Roy, Davide Venturelli, Wibe Albert de Jong

item.title: Frequency-matching quantum key distribution
item.description: arXiv:2512.05496v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables information-theoretically secure communication against eavesdropping. However, phase instability remains a challenge across many QKD applications, particularly in schemes such as twin-field QKD and measurement-device-independent QKD. The most dominant source of phase fluctuation arises from the frequency offset between independent lasers. Here we propose a method to address this issue by employing a classical photodiode to compensate for the laser frequency difference. As an application of this method, we implement this technique in a mode-pairing QKD system, achieving an error rate approaching the theoretical limit and surpassing the linear key-rate bound over a fiber distance of 296.8 km. This approach provides a practical solution for frequency matching between independent lasers and can be extended to other fields requiring precise phase stabilization.
item.dc:creator: Hao-Tao Zhu, Yizhi Huang, Abdullah Rasmita, Chao Ding, Xiangbin Cai, Haoran Zhang, Xiongfeng Ma, Weibo Gao

item.title: On the relevance of Hermitian-preserving trace-preserving linear maps in asymptotic information retrieval in quantum communication
item.description: arXiv:2512.07822v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In quantum technologies, quantum channels are essential for transmitting quantum states. Quantum channels usually introduce noise, thereby reducing the information in a state. These are mathematically described by completely positive trace-preserving linear maps that represent the generic evolution of quantum systems and are also special cases of Hermitian-preserving trace-preserving (HPTP) linear maps. Concatenating a quantum channel with another quantum channel makes it noisier and degrades its information and resource preservability. In this work, we demonstrate a physically meaningful way to compare a pair of quantum channels using Hermitian-preserving trace-preserving linear maps. Precisely, given a pair of quantum channels $\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2$ and an arbitrary unknown input state, we show that the output state of the quantum channel $\Lambda_2$ from the pair can be uniquely identified from the output statistics of the other channel $\Lambda_1$ from the pair, using some POVM, iff $\Lambda_2$ can be obtained from $\Lambda_1$ by concatenating it with a Hermitian-preserving trace-preserving linear map that is not necessarily positive. In such cases, $\Lambda_2$ may not always be obtained from $\Lambda_1$ through post-processing. The relation between these channels is a preorder, and we study its characterization in this work. In other words, we provide an operational interpretation of this preorder induced by HPTP linear maps in a communication scenario. Furthermore, we characterize the difficulty of implementing $\Lambda_2$ given that $\Lambda_1$ has already been implemented via a quantifier, namely, physical implementability. We also illustrate the implications of our results for the incompatibility of quantum devices through an example. In short, we provide valuable insights about the relevance of Hermitian-preserving trace-preserving linear maps in physically motivated settings.
item.dc:creator: Arindam Mitra, Jatin Ghai

item.title: Deep Thermalization and Measurements of Quantum Resources
item.description: arXiv:2512.09999v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum resource theories provide a unified framework for characterizing useful quantum phenomena subject to physical constraints, but are notoriously hard to assess in experimental systems. In this letter, we introduce a unified protocol for quantifying the resource-generating power of arbitrary quantum evolutions applicable to multiple resource theories. It is based on deep thermalization, which has recently gained attention for its role in the emergence of quantum state designs from partial projective measurements. Central to our approach is the use of projected ensembles, recently employed to probe deep thermalization, together with new twirling identities that allow us to directly infer the resource-generating powers of the underlying dynamics. These identities further reveal how resources build up and thermalize in generic quantum circuits. Finally, we show that quantum resources themselves undergo deep thermalization at the subsystem level, offering a complementary and another experimentally accessible route to infer the resource-generating powers. Our work connects deep thermalization to resource quantification, offering a new perspective on the essential role of various resources in generating state designs and on efficient estimation of quantum resources in experiment.
item.dc:creator: Naga Dileep Varikuti, Soumik Bandyopadhyay, Philipp Hauke

item.title: Certified bounds on optimization problems in quantum theory
item.description: arXiv:2512.17713v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Semidefinite relaxations of polynomial optimization have become a central tool for addressing the non-convex optimization problems over non-commutative operators that are ubiquitous in quantum information theory and, more in general, quantum physics. Yet, as these global relaxation methods are solved numerically, the bounds issued by the semidefinite solver can - and often do - exceed the global optimum, undermining their certifiability. To counter this issue, we introduce a framework for extracting rigorous certified bounds on non-commutative optimization problems from inexact numerical data, and apply it to several paradigmatic problems in quantum information theory. An extension to sparsity and symmetry-adapted semidefinite relaxations is also provided and compared to the general dense scheme. Our results establish rational post-processing as a practical route to reliable certification, pushing semidefinite optimization toward a certifiable standard for quantum information science.
item.dc:creator: Younes Naceur, Jie Wang, Victor Magron, Antonio Ac\'in

item.title: Geometric Complexity of Quantum Channels via Unitary Dilations
item.description: arXiv:2601.00735v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nielsen's geometric approach to quantum circuit complexity provides a Riemannian framework for quantifying the cost of implementing unitary closed-system dynamics. For open evolutions, the reduced dynamics is described by time-dependent families of quantum channels $\{\Lambda_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ admitting many inequivalent Stinespring realizations, so any meaningful complexity notion must specify which microscopic resources are counted and which transformations are treated as gauge. We develop a dilation-based geometric complexity framework that distinguishes implementation-dependent complexity, attached to a specific realization, from intrinsic channel complexity obtained by minimizing over a physically admissible class of dilations. The proposed functional is subtractive: it removes purely environmental contributions from the geometric cost of the joint unitary realization. The subtraction is derived from concise structural postulates --- closed-system consistency, environment-only neutrality, and invariance under dilation gauge transformations --- and admits a natural variational and geometric interpretation. We also define noise complexity as a companion quantity measuring the geometric deviation of a noisy implementation from a prescribed ideal closed-system evolution. In the Hilbert-Schmidt setting, we establish coherence-based lower bounds for unitary and noise complexity, prove linear time scaling under time-homogeneous dilation models, and obtain dissipator-controlled bounds in the Markovian GKSL regime. We illustrate the framework on canonical single-qubit benchmark channels: dephasing, amplitude damping, and Pauli/depolarizing noise.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Alberto Acevedo and Antonio Falc\'o 2026 J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 59 205303
item.dc:creator: Alberto Acevedo, Antonio Falc\'o

item.title: Classical Analog Emulation of Quantum Circuits via Time-Averaged Dynamic States
item.description: arXiv:2601.02977v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Between the digital and quantum paradigms lies the emerging field of quantum-inspired analog computing, in which classical waves emulate quantum circuits. We introduce wavebits -- classical wave analogs of qubits whose amplitudes are carried by physical oscillatory signals -- and show that any nonseparable N-qubit state can be encoded in 2N narrowband signals that remain locally separable at every instant; the nonseparable correlations are recovered at readout by time-averaged demodulation over auxiliary carrier frequencies, the nonseparability channels. We prove that any two-qubit gate unravels into the time-averaged tensor product of two local time-varying operators, and that arbitrary circuits are emulated with a base-frequency count scaling linearly in the number of entangling two-qubit gates, independent of qubit number for a fixed gate count. The exponential cost of the 2^N-dimensional state reappears at readout and in the averaging time of circuits with many two-qubit gates, not in circuit execution, as quantified by an analytic error bound that doubles as a hardware design rule. A mixed-signal prototype emulates Bell state generation, controlled-NOT gates, phase kickback, and Bloch-sphere rotations at fidelities above 0.99, and numerical benchmarks against exact statevectors validate the scheme for up to six qubits. The architecture is directly implementable in acoustic, photonic, and mixed-signal platforms.
item.dc:creator: Matias Miguel Castillo Valle, Tim Tuuva, Benjamin Apffel, Herv\'e Lissek, Romain Fleury, Mathieu Padlewski

item.title: Quantum circuit synthesis for fermionic excitations in coupled cluster theory
item.description: arXiv:2601.07890v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work provides a step-by-step quantum computing derivation of the unitary coupled cluster singles and doubles ansatz. We show how the structure of the ansatz emerges from fermionic algebra under unitary constraints. By explicitly connecting second quantization, Jordan-Wigner mapping, and quantum circuit synthesis, we clarify conceptual gaps between quantum physics and quantum computing implementations, particularly regarding operator locality, commutation structure, and hardware realization. We exemplify the procedure on the singles and doubles coupled cluster ansatz for the hydrogen molecule.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Hao Chen, Renata Wong

item.title: On the Redfield and Lindblad master equations
item.description: arXiv:2602.13429v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a previous work we developed a field theoretical approach to open quantum systems using condensed matter methods. In the Born approximation we derived the Redfield equation on the basis of a multi-oscillator bath, a Dyson equation, a diagrammatic expansion and a quasi-particle approximation. In addition applying a rotating wave approximation we obtained the Lindblad equation describing a proper quantum map. The issue regarding the additional rotating wave approximation was left as an open problem. The present work addresses the open problem and presents new results. We identify a discrepancy in the popular and standard Redfield equation. The discrepancy is associated with the well-known fact that the Redfield equation does not represent a proper quantum map. The discrepancy is related to the diagrammatic expansion and a consistency requirement in the quasi-particle approximation. The explicit resolution of this discrepancy is obtained by imposing energy conservation on the Born level. As a result we obtain formal equivalence between the energy-conserving Redfield equation and the Lindblad equation without invoking the rotating wave approximation. We provide a detailed mapping of the field theoretical approach to the standard microscopic derivation in the theory of open quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Hans C. Fogedby

item.title: Tensor Decomposition for Non-Clifford Gate Minimization
item.description: arXiv:2602.15285v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires substantial resources for non-Clifford gates. Their count also enters exponentially into the runtime of several classical simulation methods. We present algebraic methods for minimizing the non-Clifford CCZ (Toffoli) count in {CNOT,CCZ} phase circuits using tensor decomposition over $\mathbb{F}_2$. On standard cubic benchmarks, these methods match or improve prior automated Toffoli counts, with most instances optimized in under a minute on a single CPU. With additional computation, the decompositions provide effective initializations for existing T-count methods, improving T counts on several circuits. We also present algebraic methods for CNOT-count optimization at fixed Toffoli count. This gives competitive ancilla-free finite-field multiplication circuits and reduces the CNOT count of XOR AES S-box circuits.
item.dc:creator: Kirill Khoruzhii, Patrick Gel{\ss}, Sebastian Pokutta

item.title: QwaveMPS: An efficient open-source Python package for simulating non-Markovian waveguide-QED using matrix product states
item.description: arXiv:2602.15826v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: QwaveMPS is an open-source Python library for simulating one-dimensional quantum many-body waveguide systems using matrix product states (MPS). It provides a user-friendly interface for constructing, evolving, and analyzing quantum states and operators, facilitating studies in quantum physics and quantum information with waveguide-QED systems. This approach enables efficient, scalable simulations by focusing computational resources on the most relevant parts of the quantum system. Thus, one can study a wide range of complex dynamical interactions, including time-delayed feedback effects in the non-Markovian regime and deeply nonlinear systems, at a highly reduced computational cost compared to full Hilbert space approaches, making it both practical and convenient to model a variety of open waveguide-QED systems (in Markovian and non-Markovian regimes), treating quantized atoms and quantized photons on an equal footing. The QwaveMPS package automates the waveguide-QED-specific tensor-network operations, including construction of the time-bin evolution operator from physical parameters, the swap network required for delayed interactions, orthogonality-center and truncation management, the matrix-product factorization of $N$-photon Fock-state inputs, and the evaluation of single-time and two-time field observables (such as the second-order quantum correlation function) at chosen points along the waveguide.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Arranz Regidor, Matthew Kozma, Stephen Hughes

item.title: A rigorous hybridization of variational quantum eigensolver with classical neural network
item.description: arXiv:2602.17295v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Combining variational quantum process with classical neural learning offers a flexible route to improve ground-state estimation. We establish an integrated framework that connects neural transformations, measurement statistics, and physical stability through three requirements: self-contained training, polynomial resource scaling, and variational consistency. Its constructive realization, termed unitary variational quantum-neural hybrid eigensolver (U-VQNHE), couples a variational quantum circuit to a neural phase function through norm-preserving post-processing. The learned transformation is evaluated from measurement records, preserves the exact variational bound, and admits range-independent concentration guarantees for independent finite-shot evaluations. Complementing this construction, we characterize the statistical and representational constraints of amplitude reweighting: sampled-support mismatch can destabilize empirical normalization, while polynomial-range reweighting exactly matches only an exponentially small fraction of Haar-random target distributions from a fixed ansatz, and exact matching for structured ansatz--target pairs can require exponentially large dynamic range under specified near-tensorizability and mismatch conditions. Finite-shot simulations on Ising and disordered XYZ spin models demonstrate improved energy accuracy over the underlying variational quantum eigensolver and greater robustness than the amplitude-reweighting baselines. Together, these results provide a principled foundation for quantum--neural eigensolvers in which physical consistency, expressive capacity, and measurement cost are treated as a single design problem.
item.dc:creator: Minwoo James Kim, Kyoung Keun Park, Kyungmin Lee, Jeongho Bang, Taehyun Kim

item.title: Theory and interpretability of Quantum Extreme Learning Machines: a Pauli transfer matrix approach
item.description: arXiv:2602.18377v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum reservoir computers (QRCs) have emerged as a promising approach to quantum machine learning, since they utilize the natural dynamics of quantum systems for data processing and are simple to train. Here, we consider $n$-qubit quantum extreme learning machines (QELMs) with initial-state encoding and continuous-time reservoir dynamics. Applying the Pauli transfer matrix (PTM) formalism reveals the encoding-generated features and their linear transformation by quantum channels, and thereby provides a nonlinear vector autoregression model as an interpretable classical representation of a QELM. We show that the nonlinear information processing capacity of a QELM factorizes into the ability of the encoding to represent a given target function and the decodability of the relevant Pauli features after the effective PTM. Comparing geometric and statistical decodability reveals features that are algebraically hidden yet recoverable through data correlations. We relate the decodability of Pauli features to the spreading of measurement operators under Heisenberg evolution (Krylov growth). Focusing on the unitary channel, we discuss how structured Hamiltonians, when paired with certain observables, can impair model performance, as reflected in a low rank of the readout and the effective PTMs. We trace this effect to Hamiltonian symmetries and derive asymptotic rank estimates for symmetry-resolved observable families. Our decodability analysis disentangles the contributions of encoding, reservoir dynamics, and measurement observables, and thus provides interpretable diagnostics that can inform the design of QELMs and reduce reliance on exhaustive hyperparameter search. As a specific application, we consider forecasting nonlinear dynamical systems and show that the readout of a trained QELM closely matches the expression of the underlying flow map at leading orders.
item.dc:creator: Markus Gross, Hans-Martin Rieser

item.title: Control of Multipartite Entanglement through Anisotropy against Thermal Noise
item.description: arXiv:2602.22815v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Preserving multipartite entanglement in open many-body quantum systems is fundamentally limited by unavoidable environmental noise. We study the open-system dynamics of multipartite entanglement in an anisotropic XXZ spin chain interacting with a thermal spin bath, focusing on two states with distinct types of multipartite entanglement: the generalized GHZ and the generalized W state. Using a master-equation approach combined with the Bethe ansatz technique, we show analytically that robustness of multipartite entanglement at low temperatures can be enhanced by suitably tuning the anisotropy of the system. Our results highlight interaction-induced spectral control as a mechanism for stabilizing multipartite entanglement in quantum computing platforms.
item.dc:creator: Samudra Sur, Saikat Sur

item.title: A Scalable, Optimized Scheduler for the Active Volume Architecture
item.description: arXiv:2603.06376v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We improve the accuracy of Active Volume (AV) resource estimates by explicitly scheduling when AV blocks execute and when their reactions complete. We present a cycle-accurate scheduler that assigns each logical qubit a role in every logical cycle. The approach allows us to capture execution effects such as gate packing inefficiencies, parallelization overhead, and memory requirements. In addition, the scheduler explicitly tracks reaction latency and stale state lifetimes, rather than assuming that stale states can be absorbed into a fixed overhead. For a $4\times4$ Fermi--Hubbard test circuit, we find a transition to reaction-dominant regime at approximately $10^3$ logical qubits. Beyond $10^3$ logical qubits, stale state accumulation restricts the effective workspace and the benefit of adding more qubits is substantially decreased. Below this regime the scheduler predicts a $1.64\times$ runtime speedup relative to the previous Analytic Resource Estimators (ARE), primarily due to a $1.80\times$ reduction in average memory occupancy. We also show that parallelization and reaction latency overhead grows with available workspace, inverting the trend of the ARE model used in \cite{Caesura25}. These results provide a path toward reaction-aware analytic resource estimates and a full compilation pipeline for AV architectures. We also develop novel techniques for estimating Y state and routing demand and apply them to our test circuit. The Y state estimates result in small efficiency boost and the routing demand estimates show that routing should not bottleneck early fault-tolerant AV devices.
item.dc:creator: Sam Heavey, Athena Caesura

item.title: Quantifying entanglement in quantum thermodynamics via separability constraints
item.description: arXiv:2603.17078v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The role of quantum entanglement in thermodynamical systems remains elusive. Does entanglement result in thermodynamic advantages or does it impose fundamental limitations? Here, we unambiguously quantify the amount of heat and work in a quantum system that is due to the presence of entanglement. This is achieved by constraining the system's non-equilibrium dynamics to separable states, thereby isolating the impact entanglement has on thermodynamic effects. Unlike thermodynamic entanglement measures, which signify a loose connection between entanglement and thermodynamic properties, imposing a constraint constitutes an active intervention into a system -- answering how much of a system's thermodynamics is caused by (not correlated with) its quantumness. We benchmark our theory by applying the constrained dynamics to several multipartite systems, including quantum batteries and quantum refrigerators.
item.dc:creator: Joan Alba, Laura Ares, Jan Sperling, Julien Pinske

item.title: Bounding the entanglement of a state from its spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2604.02420v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a framework to upper bound the entanglement content of a bipartite quantum state from its spectrum alone. Using linear maps and their inverses, we derive rigorous constraints on the maximal entanglement that can be activated under global unitary transformations. We use as entanglement quantifiers the negativity and the Schmidt number; however, our framework is general and applies to any other entanglement measure. Our approach yields compact analytical sufficient criteria for bounding the entanglement of full-rank states in arbitrary dimensions and reveals new spectral constraints on Schmidt number witnesses.
item.dc:creator: Jofre Abellanet-Vidal, Guillem M\"uller-Rigat, Albert Rico, Anna Sanpera

item.title: Qurator: Scheduling Hybrid Quantum-Classical Workflows Across Heterogeneous Cloud Providers
item.description: arXiv:2604.05505v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present Qurator, a quantum-classical task scheduler that jointly optimizes queue time and circuit fidelity across heterogeneous architectures. Qurator models hybrid workloads as dynamic DAGs with explicit quantum semantics, including entanglement dependencies, synchronization barriers, no-cloning constraints, and circuit cutting and merging decisions. Fidelity is estimated through a unified logarithmic success score that reconciles incompatible calibration data from IBM, IonQ, IQM, Rigetti, AQT, Pasqal and other providers into a canonical set of gate error, readout fidelity, and decoherence terms. We evaluate Qurator on a simulator driven by four months of real queue data using circuits from the Munich Quantum Toolkit benchmark suite. Across load conditions from 5 to 35,000 quantum tasks with up to 120,000 classical tasks, Qurator stays within 1% of the highest-fidelity baseline at low load, achieves 30-75% queue time reduction at high load, all at a fidelity cost bounded by a user-specified target while improving on list and fair schedulers as well as state of the art schedulers on both metrics.
item.dc:creator: Sinan Pehlivanoglu, Ulrik de Muelenaere, Peter Kogge, Amr Sabry

item.title: Low Depth Distributed Quantum Algorithms for Unordered Database Search
item.description: arXiv:2604.14081v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Grover's algorithm accelerates unstructured database search quadratically compared to classical algorithms. In the NISQ era, distributed quantum computing can decrease circuit depth and reduce noise. In this paper, an algorithm for constructing query operators for subfunctions is proposed. By dividing the target string of the search problem into several substrings and integrating the query operator of each subfunction, a low-depth distributed exact quantum search algorithm is designed. The contributions of this paper are as follows: (1) The proposed distributed algorithm has a lower circuit depth and can mitigate error accumulation compared to distributed quantum search algorithms; (2) The target can be accurately located by the proposed distributed algorithm; (3) Experiments conducted with the quantum software MindQuantum confirm the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed distributed algorithm. Moreover, the introduction of noise to the circuit during these experiments indicates that the algorithm possesses an inherent capacity for noise resistance.
item.dc:creator: Huaijing Huang, Daowen Qiu, Ximing Hua, Xinyu Chen

item.title: Robustness Evaluation of Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks under Noise Models via System-Level Error Mitigation
item.description: arXiv:2604.17515v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) represent a promising direction within Quantum Machine Learning (QML), yet their realization on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remains constrained by decoherence, gate imperfections, crosstalk, and readout errors. This study provides a systematic evaluation of noise effects and mitigation strategies in hybrid quantum neural networks (HQNNs). Zero-Noise Extrapolation (ZNE), Digital Dynamical Decoupling (DDD), and Layerwise Richardson Extrapolation (LRE) are incorporated into end-to-end QNN training pipelines developed with PennyLane, simulated using Qiskit Aer noise models, and integrated with the Mitiq framework, while Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC) is evaluated separately under depolarizing noise due to its computational cost. Experiments conducted on the Iris dataset with five representative noise channels show that the impact of noise and the effect of mitigation are strongly dependent on the noise model and its strength. The model maintains comparatively strong performance under phase-flip and phase-damping noise, while substantial degradation is observed under high depolarizing and amplitude-damping noise. Across the evaluated mitigation methods, the observed benefits remain limited and noise-dependent: ZNE, DDD, and LRE generally follow the same degradation trends as the unmitigated baseline, while PEC shows limited gains only in the low-noise depolarizing regime. These findings highlight the need for context-specific mitigation strategies to improve the robustness of QNNs in practical NISQ settings.
item.dc:creator: Jesse Roberta Mingue Njiki, Nouhaila Innan, Alberto Marchisio, Muhammad Kashif, Jean-Michel Dricot, Muhammad Shafique

item.title: Randomized Subsystem Descent for Fermion-to-Qubit Mapping
item.description: arXiv:2604.17630v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a versatile and efficient algorithmic framework for optimizing fermion-to-qubit mappings by generalizing the idea of randomized block coordinate descent. Our greedy approach, termed Randomized Subsystem Descent, iteratively samples a tractable subsystem from the full Hamiltonian, performs optimization within the subsystem under a given metric, and then reintegrates the updated subsystem into the global operator. Restricting the optimization to a subsystem at each iteration ensures computational efficiency, bypassing the dimensional bottlenecks that usually hinder global search heuristics. We benchmark our algorithm on one- and two-dimensional lattice hopping models, the Hubbard model with up to $16 \times 16$ sites, alongside a collection of molecular electronic-structure Hamiltonians with up to $54$ modes and more than $180,000$ Pauli strings. Across all benchmarks, our method consistently provides appreciable reduction in (weighted) Pauli weight, suggesting that Randomized Subsystem Descent is a practical and scalable framework for lowering the resource overhead of finding hardware-efficient Hamiltonian encodings.
item.dc:creator: Gengzhi Yang, Di Wu, Haizhao Yang, Xiaodi Wu, Ji Liu

item.title: Entanglement and reciprocal dynamics of the Barnett and Einstein-de Haas responses in a quantum spin-rotor model
item.description: arXiv:2604.23768v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the reciprocal Barnett and Einstein--de Haas effects in an exactly solvable quantum spin--rotor model that conserves the total angular momentum. For a single spin-$1/2$, the model describes rotation-dependent spin polarization, coherent transfer of angular momentum between the spin and the rotor, and the accompanying spin--rotor entanglement. At a recoil-compensation point, all angular-momentum sectors become synchronized, allowing complete spin reversal and a one-quantum shift of an arbitrary rotor wave packet. We then extend the model to two spins coupled to the same rotor, where the shared rotational degree of freedom participates dynamically in the generation of spin--spin entanglement. The singlet forms a dark state, while the triplet sector remains coupled to the mechanical motion. At a special parameter point, the rotor returns to its original dynamical branch and disentangles from the spins, leaving behind a maximally entangled two-spin state locally equivalent to a Bell state.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Banerjee, Holger Fehske

item.title: Exploiting all ancilla outcomes in linear combinations of unitaries: low-rank recovery and quantum trapdoor functions
item.description: arXiv:2605.02986v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The linear combination of unitaries (LCU) is a fundamental quantum computing primitive used to embed non-unitary operators into larger systems via ancilla post-selection. In standard LCU implementations, only the zero-state ancilla outcome is retained, while all other measurement branches are discarded as unusable overhead. We study these discarded parts. Every computational-basis outcome of the ancilla projects the system onto a different linear combination of the target unitaries; collecting these outcome states in a matrix gives a factorization $\Phi=CX$, where $C$ is determined by the ancilla preparation and the rows of $X$ are the states $U_t|\psi\rangle$, so that $rank(\Phi)\le K$. Although this holds for any LCU circuit; to make the analysis easier, we use a simplified model circuit with Hadamard gates on the index register and a single rotation qubit in place of the coefficient preparation unitary, in which $C$ is explicit. The structure suggests two complementary applications: (i) in an explicit amplitude-access model, classical low-rank matrix completion can reconstruct the full output (including the target) from a subset of its amplitude entries, while computational basis counts provide intensities and generally require additional phase information for full complex recovery; (ii) treating $C$ as a secret key suggests a candidate quantum trapdoor function, whose security remains informal and depends on the difficulty of structured phase retrieval. The scheme thus turns the "junk" ancilla outcomes into a structured resource, possibly opening paths for further applications.
item.dc:creator: Ammar Daskin

item.title: Neural Information Causality: A Random-Access Capacity Law for Representation Learning
item.description: arXiv:2605.09316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How can a learned representation remain useful when the question it must answer is chosen only after encoding? Preserving information is essential, but does not by itself ensure access to the requested target. We address this problem by deriving "neural information causality (Neural-IC)," a representation law that connects causal access to the physically specified interface capacity. For a fresh database of independent bits, the aggregate information recoverable across later queries cannot exceed that capacity, even with pre-established quantum resources. A decomposition separates capacity slack, information organized jointly across targets, and losses in producing answers. Exhaustive evaluation of trained binary codes reveals why nearly full use of a memory's information budget can coexist with limited retrieval. In a nested Bell-correlation construction, quantum assistance improves average retrieval over the optimal classical one-bit benchmark within the same communicated budget. These results give representation learning a design principle that connects information capacity to the organization and extraction of target information. By locating the constraints on later answers, the framework can inform memory allocation, encoding objectives, and decoder outputs, providing a basis for seeking better retrieval within a fixed budget.
