item.dc:creator: Jeongho Bang, Marcin Paw{\l}owski

item.title: Freezing-Induced Interaction Engineering in Fixed-Frequency Transmon Networks
item.description: arXiv:2605.19114v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Freezing is usually used to suppress unwanted dynamics, but it can also be used to engineer interactions. We introduce freezing-induced interaction engineering, a drive-only control scheme in which a continuously driven auxiliary subsystem remains frozen while its drive-dependent state reshapes the effective Hamiltonian of neighboring degrees of freedom. We apply this idea to fixed-frequency transmon systems using a driven modulator coupled to a pivot transmon with fixed native exchange interactions to neighboring transmons. Changing only the modulator drive frequency controls the dressed resonance condition of the pivot, selectively activating a native interaction or detuning it from all neighbors. Full lab-frame simulations of multilevel transmons demonstrate this switching mechanism and show that it remains effective under finite-time frequency ramps. We further demonstrate the same control mechanism numerically in a four-transmon, two-neighbor setting, where changing only the modulator drive frequency selectively activates either neighboring native interaction or suppresses both. Repeating this local control unit along a fixed-frequency chain gives a scalable architecture for alternating layers of native iSWAP interactions.
item.dc:creator: Songbo Xie, Jiheng Duan, Sabre Kais

item.title: Towards Fair Benchmarking of Quantum Transfer Learning for Visual Classification
item.description: arXiv:2605.19417v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum Transfer Learning (QTL) offers a promising approach for visual quantum machine learning under near-term constraints, where limited qubit counts, shallow circuit depths, and costly hybrid optimization restrict end-to-end quantum training. In this setting, pretrained classical backbones can extract high-level visual features, while compact quantum modules operate as trainable classification heads. However, existing QTL results are difficult to compare because they often differ in datasets, preprocessing, backbone settings, qubit budgets, circuit designs, optimization choices, and reporting protocols. This work presents a controlled benchmarking methodology for evaluating representative QTL methods under a unified transfer-learning pipeline. The benchmark compares DQN-QTL, QPIE-QTL, AE-CQTL, PVCQTL, and ED-QTL under shared preprocessing rules, frozen-backbone settings, training conditions, and reporting metrics. The evaluation focuses on Fashion-MNIST and Hymenoptera Ants vs. Bees as the two main datasets, while CIFAR-10 is used to provide additional configuration-level evidence on a harder natural-image task. Beyond predictive performance, the benchmark analyzes circuit size, trainable parameters, quantum parameters, training time, and architectural sensitivity to qubit count and circuit depth. The results show that no single QTL family dominates across all settings: performance depends on the dataset, encoding strategy, circuit design, and computational cost. These findings highlight the need for resource-aware QTL evaluation and provide guidance for selecting hybrid quantum-classical transfer models under near-term resource constraints.
item.dc:creator: Nouhaila Innan, Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

item.title: Impurity-induced loss bursts from anomalous scale-free localization in a non-Hermitian dissipative lattice
item.description: arXiv:2605.21034v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We identify anomalous scale-free localization and associated impurity-induced loss bursts in a non-Hermitian dissipative cross-stitch lattice. By a local basis rotation, the model is mapped onto an effective non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger lattice, where local impurities act as tunable effective boundaries. For the parameter choice considered here, the impurity-free periodic-boundary-condition point is reached at $\eta=1$. Tuning $\eta$ away from this point drives the system through generalized-boundary-condition regimes toward two effective open-boundary-condition-like limits at $\eta\to0$ and $\eta\to\infty$. For finite $\eta\notin\{0,1\}$, the loop-sector spectra remain separated from the real-energy axis, while the corresponding eigenstates exhibit scale-free localization pinned by the impurity. Unlike conventional impurity-induced scale-free localization, the Lyapunov exponent depends explicitly on the eigenenergy, making the localization strength eigenstate dependent. We further show that this anomalous eigenmode structure produces an impurity-induced loss burst: The long-time integrated dissipation probability develops a pronounced local enhancement relative to the surrounding background near an impurity-generated effective boundary, even when the initial wave packet is prepared far away. In the single-impurity case, the burst region consists of the impurity site and its adjacent effective-boundary site, and the effect occurs without imaginary-gap closing. For multiple impurities, local burst regions emerge around all impurities, while the dominant burst boundary is selected by the initial wave-packet position and the nonreciprocal drift direction. These results connect anomalous scale-free localization with controllable dissipation dynamics in non-Hermitian lattices.
item.dc:creator: Hui Liu, Zhihao Xu

item.title: Fate of Quantum Scars and Chaos-Assisted Tunneling under Dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2605.22953v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum scars enable memory and recurrent dynamics, but their fate under dissipation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that distinct quantum scars can respond qualitatively differently to the same dissipative channel. We consider a collective spin model coupled to a lossy cavity and, guided by its classical limit, identify scars associated with two unstable structures: a saddle point on a dissipation-free invariant manifold with vanishing cavity field and an unstable superradiant fixed point with finite photon occupation. The former is immune to photon loss in the classical limit and exhibits persistent quantum revivals, whereas the latter couples directly to the dissipative channel, but exhibits slow dynamics. Remarkably, the superradiant scar also supports chaos-assisted quantum tunneling between two symmetry-related, macroscopically distinct semiclassical configurations, despite the presence of dissipation. Our results identify an experimentally accessible setting for exploring dissipative scarring and chaos-assisted tunneling in cavity QED.
item.dc:creator: Debabrata Mondal, Sohan Pati, Lea F. Santos, S. Sinha

item.title: Homomorphic Quantum Error Correction
item.description: arXiv:2605.25692v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the algebraic compatibility between quantum homomorphic encryption and stabilizer quantum error correction in an honest-but-curious model, restricting the encryption to the transversal block-Pauli mask $(X^aZ^b)^{\otimes n}$ controlled by two secret key bits $a$ and $b$. We prove a necessary and sufficient criterion for an $[[n,1,d]]$ stabilizer code to remain compatible with this mask, namely that the transversal $X$ and $Z$ operators commute with every stabilizer generator, and we specialize it to a classical-code criterion for Calderbank--Shor--Steane codes. Combining code-space preservation with the logical action of the mask, every stabilizer code falls, with respect to each of the two transversal mask operators, into exactly one of three classes: incompatible, compatible but trivially acting, or compatible with a nontrivial logical Pauli action; the two operators need not fall into the same class. We verify this classification by exact symplectic computation for rotated and planar surface codes, toric codes, triangular and toric color codes, the $[[15,1,3]]$ code and several small codes, and find that the class is fixed by the lattice size and the boundary presentation rather than by the topological phase: the surface-code family realizes all three classes, whereas color codes realize only the two compatible ones. For encrypted computation we show that the Shor code does not implement the logical $T$ gate by a transversal $T^{\otimes 9}$, whereas suitable triorthogonal codes do so up to a Clifford correction. We formulate logical-Pauli masking as a code-independent algebraic template. Syndrome extraction and recovery are key-independent whenever the mask preserves the code space, so that the client only needs the block size and the class of the code to decrypt.
item.dc:creator: Kornikar Sen, Miguel A. Martin-Delgado

item.title: PauLIB: HPC Strategies for Pauli-Arithmetic-Based Quantum Computing Workloads and Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2605.25974v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As quantum devices become accelerators within classical HPC deployments, the efficiency of the classical partition becomes critical. Workloads such as Hamiltonian manipulation, observable backpropagation, and Pauli-based compilation reduce to bulk arithmetic on Pauli strings and sums. We present HPC strategies for this arithmetic, demonstrated in PauLIB, a header-only C++20 library: a bit-packed binary symplectic representation reducing Pauli multiplication to a bitwise XOR and population count; a sorted, struct-of-arrays layout replacing hash maps and exposing contiguous word arrays to SIMD units and GPU warps; and deterministic OpenMP parallelism with race-free output partitioning. These strategies deliver orders-of-magnitude higher throughput and smaller memory footprint than Qiskit and PauliEngine, plus a speedup from a CUDA outer-product kernel on an H100. Two case studies, g-sim and truncated Pauli propagation, inherit these gains and scale unchanged from a desktop Arm CPU to a 72-core HPC Arm server. PauLIB is open source with C++ and Python interfaces.
item.dc:creator: Florian Kr\"otz

item.title: Quantum digital simulations of time-domain semiconductor spectroscopy in the semi-classical approximation
item.description: arXiv:2606.04295v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a digital quantum simulation framework for ultrafast optical spectroscopy of semiconductor materials. The framework is based on Brillouin-zone discretization and is designed as a quantum alternative to classical simulations based on the semiconductor Bloch equations. Its current capabilities include quantum simulations of linear absorption and optical gain, incorporating Lorentzian broadening, finite-temperature band-filling effects, and reduced-dimensionality effects. Comparison with classical simulations of GaAs within the single-particle approximation demonstrates quantitative agreement in the noiseless limit. The inclusion of realistic hardware noise characteristic of NISQ-era quantum computers effectively manifests as an additional source of scattering, resulting in increased spectral broadening. We also show that the linear optical response, including many-body interactions treated within the Hartree-Fock approximation, can be mapped onto a system of coupled classical oscillators. Under certain assumptions about the query complexity of the oscillator couplings, this system exhibits a provable quantum advantage, as demonstrated in [Phys. Rev. X 13, 041041 (2023)]. Beyond the Hartree-Fock approximation, classical simulations based on many-body quantum kinetic equations face the so-called hierarchy problem, whereas the algorithmic complexity of the quantum simulations remains unchanged, offering a promising approach to overcoming this challenge.
item.dc:creator: Mykhailo Klymenko, Bahar Goldozian, Thong Hoang, Jared H. Cole, Muhammad Usman

item.title: QPredSGG: Hybrid Quantum Predicate Learning for Long-Tailed Scene Graph Generation
item.description: arXiv:2606.04689v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scene Graph Generation (SGG) requires relational reasoning over objects and their interactions, but performance is constrained by long-tail predicate imbalance. Classical SGG models rely on dataset statistics, leading to biased predictions toward frequent relations rather than fine-grained semantic predicates. Although debiasing improves mean recall, predicate classification in existing frameworks still relies on high-dimensional classical decision modules with high parameter overhead. This work introduces a resource-efficient hybrid quantum predicate classifier for SGG by replacing the classical predicate head in the CFEN with a QP-Head trained using class-balanced WCE. To the best of our knowledge, this work is among the first evaluations of a hybrid quantum architecture for scene graph predicate classification on Visual Genome 150. We evaluate the impact of qubit count, encoding strategy, entangling topology, and circuit depth. Under a 4-qubit configuration using Amplitude Embedding and Strongly Entangling Layers, the QP-Head projects 4096-dimensional pair features into a 16-dimensional quantum input while using 96 trainable quantum parameters. Operating within this compressed representation space under WCE training, it achieves strong long-tail recognition, reaching a peak mR@100 of 57.25% compared to the 41.1% mR@100 reported in the CFEN baseline under standard training. Protocol-matched ablations indicate that the primary advantage of the quantum head lies in extreme representational compactness rather than an accuracy gain over full-dimensional weighted classical heads: it achieves global recall within 0.19pp of the 2048-dimensional WCE classical baseline while operating from a 128x smaller head feature space. Scaling to 8 qubits maintains robust long-tail performance (55.38% mR@100 with 384 quantum parameters), while depth analysis highlights expressibility-latency trade-offs.
item.dc:creator: Prerana Ramkumar, Nouhaila Innan, Muhammad Shafique

item.title: Dynamical Decoupling using Universal Optimal Tracking
item.description: arXiv:2606.21762v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a widely used and resource-efficient technique for error suppression, but conventional DD relies on periodically repeating a short pulse block to refocus the qubit state during idle periods. Imperfections in this block cause residual errors to accumulate, ultimately degrading state recovery over long idle times. Here, we introduce a universal optimal tracking approach that extends the original tracking concept to a fully state-independent setting for designing DD sequences. By monitoring the qubit's evolution at predefined waypoints during optimization, the method dynamically compensates residual errors while preserving regular refocusing. Experimental demonstrations on a superconducting-qubit platform confirm the suppression of error accumulation under static control imperfections, in agreement with numerical predictions. Complementary simulations further show that optimal-tracking-based sequences maintain strong performance under time-dependent noise. These results establish optimal tracking as a practical and hardware-agnostic approach to designing short, robust DD sequences suitable for noisy quantum devices.
item.dc:creator: Amit Devra, Emanuel Malvetti, Niklas J. Glaser, Abhishek Agarwal, Ivan Rungger, Santana Lujan, Max Werninghaus, Stefan Filipp, L\'eo Van Damme, Steffen J. Glaser

item.title: Quantum Imaging via Kurtosis-Difference Weighted Covariance on 2D Camera
item.description: arXiv:2606.31005v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Camera-based quantum imaging detects spatially correlated photon pairs from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC). Conventional covariance methods typically require tens of thousands of frames to extract weak correlations from noise. While thick crystals can increase photon flux, they generate photon pairs from multiple emission positions within the crystal, producing multiple correlation centers with complex pairing geometries. In addition, conventional covariance methods assume a single pre-selected correlation center and cannot fully exploit these distributed correlations. We demonstrate that kurtosis difference, a fourth-order statistic measuring tail similarity, effectively discriminates correlated pixel pairs even when correlation coefficients remain low. Weighting covariance by an exponential function of absolute kurtosis difference can select symmetric pixels while preserving true coincidences. This kurtosis weighting automatically identifies correlated pairs within a broad search region and accommodates multiple pairing geometries without requiring precise correlation center calibration. At 5000 frames, our method yields a contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) exceeding 7, whereas standard covariance remains below 2. Compared with standard covariance, the method reduces the acquisition time by 40-fold and could enable practical quantum imaging in sparse correlated-photon regimes.
item.dc:creator: Zhe He, Yanli Shi, Hui Wu, Qun Cao, Weidong Zheng, Zheng Cui

item.title: Operational boundaries, threshold conditions, and self-quenching in single-emitter microcavity lasers
item.description: arXiv:2606.31239v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We theoretically examine the emission dynamics of a three-level cascade single-emitter microcavity laser using the open-system Lindblad master equation. In our numerical simulations, we expand the Hilbert space dimensions to obtain converged observables free from truncation artifacts. We notice that the intracavity field builds up continuously to a peak value of $\langle n_p \rangle_{\rm max}$, bypassing the sharp thermodynamic thresholds of conventional ensemble lasers. By tracking individual radiative rates and for the selected set of parameters, we isolate a physical threshold at a normalized pump rate of $\Gamma/\gamma_{12} \approx 2.45$, where net stimulated emission overcomes spontaneous noise. Crucially, comparing these numerical master equation solutions against factorized semiclassical models reveals that mean-field approximations omit a vital light-matter correlation drag force, leading to a substantial overestimation of the peak field intensity by more than 10\%. We notice that the transient Wigner function undergoes complete phase diffusion into a radially symmetric ring due to the absence of a phase-locking ensemble. Furthermore, steady-state noise calculations confirm that discrete incoherent pumping fluctuations restrict the field to strictly super-Poissonian statistics (with the Mandel parameter $Q > 0$ and the second-order coherence function with zero delay $g^{(2)}(0) > 1$), establishing the classical shot-noise limit as a strict lower bound. At high pumping rates, population trapping in the upper level creates an excitation bottleneck that suppresses the cavity field and causes self-quenching. Our results provide an essential baseline for optimizing solid-state quantum dot and color-center nanophotonic architectures for lasing as well as for the generation of non-classical states of light.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Gospodinov, Celia Powers, Imran M. Mirza

item.title: Accuracy, Decision Risk, and Sampling Cost in Quantum Error Mitigation
item.description: arXiv:2607.02888v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum error mitigation estimates expectation values that are often used to select or rank candidates. We study how estimation accuracy, decision risk and sampling cost are related in these tasks. The joint law of residual differences determines the risk of a shift-invariant decision; in Gaussian regimes, effective margins and their covariance provide a computable representation. This connects mitigation maps, shared measurement records and shot allocation, and yields an extrapolation design criterion under certified margins. Finite-shot QAOA-MaxCut controls illustrate two forms of this relationship: a positive affine CDR correction reduces mean-squared error while preserving rankings, whereas signed PEC sampling reduces mean-squared error and increases selection failures at equal evaluation cost. A retrospective, oracle-assisted study of 48 landscapes compares Gaussian-risk and MSE-based method selection using separate fitting, selection and evaluation samples. At the primary total shot budget, with learning amortized over 20 decisions per landscape, failure rates are $0.3083$ for Gaussian-risk selection, $0.4719$ for MSE selection and $0.2333$ for unmitigated estimation. These comparisons describe how uncertainty in candidate differences and the allocation of measurements between learning and evaluation jointly enter the assessment of mitigation.
item.dc:creator: Vicenzo Scavino Alfaro

item.title: Decoherence of a quantum magneto-oscillator: Effect of field-bath interaction
item.description: arXiv:2607.11137v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the quantum dissipative dynamics of a charged magneto-oscillator(CMO) coupled to a heat bath of harmonic oscillators in the presence of an additional field-bath interaction. The problem is formulated within the framework of the generalized quantum Langevin equation, where the external confining potential modifies the random force correlations and the memory kernel of the environment, and the effective spring constant. Using the corresponding non-Markovian master equation, we examine the influence of the field-bath coupling on the temporal decay of the reduced density matrix of the system. We show that the additional interaction leads to an enhancement of the decoherence rate by altering the dissipative response of the bath. Thus our results shed light on the role of field-bath coupling in the quantum to classical transition of a CMO. The resulting fluctuation-dissipation relation is analyzed, and the position autocorrelation, position-velocity correlation and velocity autocorrelation are obtained explicitly. The dependence of these experimentally accessible quantities on the field-bath coupling parameter is discussed. We outline an experimental proposal for testing our theoretical predictions. The study sheds light on reservoir engineering which is central to quantum technologies.
item.dc:creator: Koushik Mandal, Suraka Bhattacharjee, Supurna Sinha

item.title: Inherent interpretability provides inherent value in quantum machine learning
item.description: arXiv:2607.13827v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The field of quantum machine learning (QML) evolved to value models believed to most directly rival those providing utility in classical ML, namely large-scale neural networks. This pursuit of quantum neural-network analogues has produced important theoretical insights for expressivity and trainability at scale; however, due to our inability to conduct large-scale empirical studies, this direction has contributed to skepticism that QML will provide a compelling application for quantum computers. In the meantime, classical ML has been learning a hard lesson with respect to deploying un-interpretable neural networks in the wild: model interpretability matters for human adoption. We adopt this broader ML perspective to encourage a research direction in QML that prioritizes discovering and understanding tools from quantum information theory that applied ML researchers can use to construct inherently interpretable models: models with intentional mathematical structure that guarantees domain-aligned behavior. We first exemplify this research direction through a thread of work in a neighboring area---Bayesian ML. Specifically, we discuss an efficient mathematical tool that emerged from a connection between Gaussian processes and Bayesian linear models, which has since been widely studied and used by applied researchers for problem-specific model design. We then discuss how prior QML research can be reframed as progress towards this direction, despite having been pursued with different goals in mind. Finally, we propose an initial sketch of future work in this direction, with the broader aim of better supporting the needs of applied ML researchers.
item.dc:creator: Kaitlin Gili, Zachary P. Bradshaw

item.title: New bound on $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting Bell locality of a nonseparable Werner state
item.description: arXiv:2607.18050v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In many quantum applications it is important to know whether or not a Bell nonlocal two-qudit state exhibits its nonlocality under correlation scenarios with some given numbers $S_{1},S_{2}\geq1$ of generalized quantum measurements at two sites. In the present article, we find analytically a new general condition sufficient for a nonseparable Werner state with a dimension $d\leq\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\}$ to satisfy all Bell inequalities under every $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting correlation scenario with outcomes of an arbitrary spectral type, discrete or continuous $-$ that is, to be $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting Bell local, for short. For a variety of measurement settings $S_{1}, S_{2}$, this new general bound is beyond (i) Werner's and Barrett's locality bounds for a nonseparable Werner state and (ii) the related result by Johnson and Viola [Phys. Rev. A 88, 032323 (2013)] on "sharability" of this state. When specialized to $d = 2$ and $\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\} = 2, 3$, our new general bound improves upon the corresponding results by Terhal et. al. in [Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 157903 (2003)], moreover, for $d=\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\} = 2$, it reduces exactly to the bound derived for this case via the CHSH inequality. We prove also explicitly in operator terms the result of Terhal et. el. that every nonseparable Werner state with a dimension $d >\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\}$ is $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting Bell local. The new results presented in this article are important for both the theory of Bell nonlocality and quantum applications based on this fundamental concept.
item.dc:creator: Elena R. Loubenets

item.title: Limitations on Joint Coherence Transfer in Quantum Thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2608.11872v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coherences between different energy levels are strongly constrained by thermodynamics. Here we ask whether several coherence transfers that can be optimized separately can also be optimized simultaneously by the same thermodynamic process. Using an energy-resolved Stinespring representation of thermal operations, we express elementary transfer amplitudes as inner products of bath-weighted vectors. Joint saturation imposes collinearity and phase-closure conditions on these vectors, which must all arise from one energy-preserving system--bath unitary. This gives necessary compatibility conditions for arbitrary finite-dimensional Hamiltonians. We show that joint incompatibility persists in a system with both degenerate and nondegenerate energy levels: rigorous computer-assisted semidefinite-program bounds, combined with explicit thermal constructions, prove that three individual thermal optima cannot be approached simultaneously. We then determine how well different coherences can be protected when their optima are incompatible. For a four-level family at infinite temperature, we obtain the complete closed retention region and the cost of balancing the coherences relative to their individual optima. At positive temperature, covariance and Gibbs preservation permit joint retention that no thermal operation can approach. Finite-bath constructions and certified semidefinite relaxations bound the balanced thermal performance. When two coherences carry independent phases, these bounds describe simultaneous preservation of interference visibility and phase Fisher information.
item.dc:creator: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski, Micha{\l} Studzi\'nski

item.title: The Entanglement Content of Quantum Measurement Bases
item.description: arXiv:2608.21185v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bell-state measurements are essential ingredients in many protocols for quantum information processing, ranging from quantum teleportation and dense coding to entanglement distribution in quantum networks. Their power relies on the fact that they are measurements in an entangled basis of a two-particle system and that the used Bell-state basis can be generated from a single Bell state by local unitary transformations. How can these measurements be generalized to more particles? We develop a general framework for this state-to-measurement problem: We introduce a hierarchy of classes of measurement bases, distinguished by the local transformations the parties may use for their generation from a single state. This leads to a generalization of the concept of maximally entangleable (or weighted hypergraph) states and the identification of a novel maximally entangled basis of four qubits, being a candidate for data-hiding tasks or distillation protocols. Finally, we prove that not all forms of entanglement can be encoded in an entire measurement basis.
item.dc:creator: Jef Pauwels, Otfried G\"uhne

item.title: Measurements on the separated subsystems of an entangled state
item.description: arXiv:2609.04178v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The entangled states of composite quantum systems are well studied. The particle-like nature of these systems also means that, while entangled, they can be physically separated and measurements performed on the separated subsystems. Measurements on the separated subsystems A and B should pertain to vectors in the local Hilbert space of each subsystem, but to date it has not been clear how to elucidate the relevant states of the separated subsystems because it is not obvious how to resolve them from states given in the tensor product basis, except for the separable states. Here it is shown that the projections of any general entangled state that are detected by measurements on the separated subsystems can be obtained considering the corresponding (cosets of) states in the free vector space from which the tensor product space is defined. The result eliminates the need to invoke random collapse, and from this perspective nonlocality arises because of the way measurements on each separated subsystem projects possible measurement outcomes.
item.dc:creator: Gregory D. Scholes

item.title: Minimum Cardinalities of Multipartite Unextendible Product Bases
item.description: arXiv:2609.05657v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In quantum information theory, the state space of a multipartite quantum system is modeled by a tensor product. In the tensor-product space $\C^{d_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\C^{d_p}$, a nonzero vector is a \emph{product state} if it can be written as $\ket{\varphi_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\ket{\varphi_p}$ with $\ket{\varphi_j}\in\C^{d_j}\setminus\{0\}$. An \emph{unextendible product basis} (UPB) is a finite family of pairwise orthogonal product states such that no nonzero product state is orthogonal to all of them. UPBs play a key role in investigating quantum entanglement and nonlocal phenomena. Finding a smallest UPB is a natural extremal problem: it asks how few pairwise orthogonal product states suffice to prevent any further product state from being added. The general minimum-size problem for UPBs has been studied for over two decades since the seminal work of Alon and Lov\'asz. Let $f_m(d_1,\ldots,d_p)$ be the minimum cardinality of a UPB in the space, and let \(f_{LB}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)=1+\sum_{j=1}^{p}(d_j-1)\) be the natural lower bound. Alon and Lov\'asz determined exactly when \(f_m\) attains the lower bound \(f_{LB}\), but the obstructed multipartite cases remained open in general. We prove a stabilization theorem: for every non-all-qubit system with $p\ge3$, whenever the natural lower bound $f_{LB}$ is unattainable, the true minimum is exactly $f_{LB}+1$. Precisely, if the number of even local dimensions $d_i$ is positive and even, and at least one local dimension is greater than two, then \(f_m(d_1,\ldots,d_p)=f_{LB}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)+1\). The proof is built on a unified graph-theoretic framework. Our result, together with earlier work, settles the minimum size problem for UPBs in all finite quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Chenhao Wang

item.title: Subsystem self-correction of the GKP qubit
item.description: arXiv:2609.07702v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Passive quantum error correction, also known as self-correction, is a holy grail in quantum information science. Recent theoretical advances suggest that the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) code can exhibit self-correction properties, positioning it as a candidate for the realization of self-correcting quantum memories. In this article, we provide a self-contained derivation of the self-correcting behavior of the ideal GKP Hamiltonian, manifested in the Arrhenius type scaling of the logical lifetime, from a quantum-information perspective based on the subsystem code decomposition. When coupling through the physical quadrature $q$ and $p$, the detailed-balance jump operators decompose into a dominant part acting only on the gauge subsystem and a boundary term that acts non-trivially on the logical qubit. The boundary term is then exponentially suppressed by the Gibbs weights near the edge of the modular cells. In contrast to spin-based quantum memories such as the two-dimensional surface code, the GKP Hamiltonian realizes an effective string tension in modular phase space, whereby the energy cost increases as an error approaches the boundary of a logical sector.
item.dc:creator: Brian Chung Hang Cheung, Lasse Bj{\o}rn Kristensen, Frederik Nathan, Michael Kastoryano

item.title: Exact computation of quantum wave functions for nonlinear potentials
item.description: arXiv:2609.14480v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent work shows that the Schr\"odinger equation can be solved exactly based only on classical least action. The computation is based on first computing the multi-valued action solutions of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, computing the classical propagated density along all stationary action multipaths, and finally constructing the exact kernel and wave function based on these classical multi-valued quantities alone. The method requires that the propagated classical square root density along each stationary action path is harmonic, as is the case for basic examples such as e.g., the double-slit, quantum tunneling, or the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen experiment. For more complex cases, residual Bohm-like quantum potentials along each stationary action path can be eliminated through a time-rescaling. This paper proposes an extended version of the above construction which avoids the need for time-rescaling even in the most general cases. This is achieved by introducing in the Hamilton-Jacobi equation a real viscosity term, which classically simply corresponds to replacing a lumped parameter model with a continuum model including a volumetric stress tensor. This keeps the earlier construction unchanged, except that the real stationary action multipaths are now real stationary viscous action multipaths defined with respect to an associated modified Lagrangian. As in the earlier version, the construction extends straightforwardly to the special and general relativistic contexts, thus describing in a common language the quantum, classical, and relativistic cases. Note that the global Bohm potential term in the lumped Hamilton-Jacobi equation associated with a Madelung transform does not have a classical equivalent, while the volumetric stress tensor term in our viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equation directly represents the real paths of a classical deformed particle field.
item.dc:creator: Winfried Loghmiller, Jean-Jacques Slotine

item.title: Unconditional Security of Discrete-Modulated CV-QKD from Infinite-Dimensional MEAT
item.description: arXiv:2609.16105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Discrete-Modulated (DM) Continuous-Variable (CV) Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is an experimentally attractive approach to quantum cryptography, offering high key rates over metropolitan-scale distances while relying on state-of-the-art telecom infrastructure. However, a fundamental gap has remained between this experimental promise and rigorous security: for more than two decades, DM CV-QKD has lacked a complete composable finite-size security proof against coherent attacks. Existing works either restrict the adversary to collective attacks, impose additional finite-dimensional assumptions, apply only to specific modulation formats, or fail to recover the known asymptotic rates. Here, we resolve this longstanding problem by establishing the first complete composable finite-size security proof for DM CV-QKD protocols against coherent attacks, incorporating imperfect detectors and both fixed- and variable-length protocol variants. Our proof introduces two central results of broader interest: an infinite-dimensional marginal-constrained entropy accumulation theorem (iMEAT) and a rigorous dimension-reduction technique that makes the infinite-dimensional security bounds numerically tractable. The resulting key rates recover the known asymptotic rates and outperform established finite-size bounds based on collective attacks, while yielding positive key rates beyond $70$km for experimentally relevant block sizes and parameters. Thus, our work closes a longstanding gap and places an experimentally attractive class of CV-QKD protocols on a rigorous composable security footing and provides a pathway towards their practical deployment.
item.dc:creator: Lars Kamin, Ian George, John Burniston, Florian Kanitschar

item.title: Approximate synthesis of general single-qubit unitaries over the Clifford+$\sqrt{T}$ gate set
item.description: arXiv:2609.16659v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the standard Clifford+$T$ gate set, deterministic, ancilla-free synthesis now attains the minimal $T$-count for general single-qubit unitaries (Morisaki et al., arXiv:2510.05816). The $\sqrt{T}$ gate rotates by half the angle of $T$, generating a finer lattice of implementable operations. Access to this magic state is expected to lower the cost of deterministic and ancilla-free synthesis of general single-qubit unitaries (Kliuchnikov et al., arXiv:2203.10064), but no direct Clifford+$\sqrt{T}$ algorithm existed for this case. We provide one by extending the integer lattice-point enumeration method of Morisaki et al. We adopt a resource state cost model based on the magic-state catalysis approach of Gidney and Fowler (arXiv:1812.01238). On Haar-random targets synthesized to precisions ranging from $\varepsilon=10^{-3}$ to $10^{-8}$, the cost of Clifford+$\sqrt{T}$ circuits scales as $2.4\log_2(1/\varepsilon)$ compared to $3.0\log_2(1/\varepsilon)$ for $T$-count-optimal Clifford+$T$ circuits. Once a one-time catalyst state is amortized, the Clifford+$\sqrt{T}$ circuits are never costlier than their Clifford+$T$ counterparts.
item.dc:creator: Mathias Weiden, Jae Won Kim, Justin Kalloor, John Kubiatowicz, Costin Iancu

item.title: Eigenvalue-by-Eigenvalue Comparison of a Sierra--Rodr\'iguez-Laguna-Type Spectrum with the Riemann Zeros
item.description: arXiv:2609.23353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the self-adjoint extension of the Sierra--Rodr\'iguez-Laguna (SR) $H=xp$-type Hamiltonian $\widehat H_{SR}$. Its discrete spectrum is fixed by the equation $\mathrm{Re}\!\left[e^{-i\theta/2}K_{1/2+iE/2}(2\pi)\right]=0$. We solve this equation numerically for $\theta=1.417\pi$ and obtain the first 606 eigenvalues $E_n$. We compare them, one by one, with the ordinates $\gamma_n$ of the first 606 nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Using the steepest-descent (saddle-point) method for the modified Bessel function, together with the Riemann--von Mangoldt formula, we derive a closed-form prediction for $E_n-\gamma_n$ in terms of the Lambert-$W$ function: $E_n-\gamma_n\simeq(\theta-\pi/4)/[1+W(n/e)]$, which decays only like $1/\ln n$. Here the $n$-th numerical root corresponds to the $(n-2)$-th root of the asymptotic quantization condition. The leading-order phase of $K_{1/2+iE/2}(2\pi)$ agrees with a known rigorous asymptotic formula for modified Bessel functions of large imaginary order. The prediction is checked against the first $10^5$ tabulated zeta zeros (A.~Odlyzko): the measured coefficient of $1/[1+W(n/e)]$ is $3.666$ (mean) and $3.667$ (median) for $n\ge10^3$, in agreement with $\theta-\pi/4=3.666$. The scatter of $E_n-\gamma_n$ around this smooth curve comes from the fluctuating term $S(T)$ of the zero-counting function, which the spectrum $E_n$ does not contain.
item.dc:creator: Mi-Ra Hwang, Eylee Jung, MuSeong Kim, DaeKil Park

item.title: The coupler Eve did not monitor: non-signalling reports from interacting cavities
item.description: arXiv:2610.09103v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Eve receives genuine average photon counts from two opaque devices, finds input-independent single-party report distributions, and sees little activity in a specified leakage monitor. Do these observations establish physical isolation? We construct a cavity-based counterexample. Independently operated controls activate a shared interaction after the inputs arrive. Internal block measurements yield a CHSH score $S=13/4$ for four repetitions, approaching $4$ for large blocks. A fresh shared random bit symmetrizes the binary results without changing their parity; local preparation of vacuum or one-photon output states then produces truthful photon-number reports with exactly non-signalling marginals. A dispersive-bus model also permits weak monitored leakage; an illustrative dissipative calculation gives $S\simeq3.1702$ with ideal output encoding. These scores exceed $2\sqrt2$ because the devices interact during their response, not because quantum mechanics is violated. The construction separates honest measurement, non-signalling reported statistics, and causal isolation, while making the additional randomness, preparation, and monitoring assumptions explicit.
item.dc:creator: Yueying Wu

item.title: Dynamical Lie Algebras for Fixed-Gate Quantum Ans\"atze
item.description: arXiv:2610.13709v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parameterized Quantum Circuits have emerged as a central framework for variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ regime, with major applications in quantum simulation, combinatorial optimization, and, more recently, quantum machine learning (QML). By developing a new approach for computing dynamical Lie algebras associated with quantum circuits combining parametrized gates and non-parametrized entangling gates, we aim to extend the applicability of recent algebraic results to architectures that are actually used in quantum machine learning.
item.dc:creator: Orlane Zang, Daniel Juteau, Tony Quertier, Gr\'egoire Barru\'e

item.title: Breakdown of thermalization in quantum spin systems with long-range interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15530v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum thermalization of closed systems -- i.e. the relaxation of local properties to their thermodynamic value along the Hamiltonian evolution -- is generically expected in non-integrable systems at finite energy density. In this work we show that quantum spin systems with at least one spin component coupled through long-range ferromagnetic interactions, and a second spin component coupled to a field, cannot in general thermalize to a paramagnetic state whenever they have a finite, negative energy per spin. The long-range interactions we consider decay as a power law of the distance, $\sim r^{-\alpha}$ with $\alpha < d$, where $d$ is the number of spatial dimensions of the system. The lack of thermalization is generic to an infinite family of Hamiltonians, and it is not associated to any form of integrability. It can instead be understood by the anomalous features of the thermodynamics of the system in the paramagnetic phase, which cannot be reflected in the properties of the eigenstates. This leads to a breakdown of eigenstate typicality and of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Interestingly, the non-thermal states emerging at long times in the dynamics display long-range multipartite entanglement, elevating the breakdown of thermalization to a resource.
item.dc:creator: Filippo Caleca, Fabio Mezzacapo, Tommaso Roscilde

item.title: On the Increase of Boltzmann Entropy in Closed Macroscopic Quantum Systems
item.description:
arXiv:2610.18553v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a closed macroscopic quantum system in a pure state $\psi$ evolving unitarily with Hamiltonian $H$ in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}$. Following von Neumann, we assume a decomposition of $\mathscr{H}$ into mutually orthogonal subspaces $\mathscr{H}_{
u}$, where each $
u$ represents a macro state, and $\mathscr{H}_
u$ contains the pure states compatible with $
u$. We define the quantum Boltzmann entropy for a macro state $
u$ as $S_\mathrm{qB}(
u) = k_{\mathrm{B}} \log \dim \mathscr{H}_{
u}$, where $k_\mathrm{B}$ is the Boltzmann constant. Goldstein et al. [http://arxiv.org/abs/1903.11870] have suggested, as a version of the second law of thermodynamics, that $S_\mathrm{qB}$ predominantly increases with time for realistic macroscopic systems. Here, we discuss precise versions of this statement and confirm them for several simple models of $H$ and $\mathscr{H}_
u$.
item.dc:creator: Cedric Igelspacher, Roderich Tumulka

item.title: Scalable Tomography of Coherent Noise via Stabilizer-Code Polarization
item.description: arXiv:2610.19779v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coherent errors accumulate linearly rather than diffusively, making them invisible to Pauli-twirl-based characterization. This poses a central challenge for quantum error correction, yet its characterization typically requires multi-qubit process tomography whose cost grows exponentially with system size. We show that measurement-free error correction projects arbitrary few-qubit coherent noise onto a fixed single-logical-qubit effective channel, enabling tomography at constant cost. Exploiting the polarization effects of bit-flip and phase-flip codes, we construct a concatenated effective-channel fingerprint and prove, by a parity-based contradiction argument, that the observation map is globally injective over a prescribed coherent-noise family; hence the underlying noise parameters are uniquely recovered without any sparsity or low-rank assumptions. We further corroborate the theoretical guarantee by a synthetic numerical test: over 500 randomly sampled points in the compact parameter domain, the $64\times11$ Jacobian of the concatenated fingerprint maintains full column rank with a strictly positive smallest singular value in every case, confirming that all 11 parameter directions remain first-order identifiable throughout the region. The recovered coherent noise model can be fed into decoding algorithms; relative to independent noise priors, we expect this to reduce the logical error rate for surface-code decoders. The protocol offers a scalable route to coherent-noise identification whenever the noise admits a moderate-dimensional parameterization.
item.dc:creator: Long Huang

item.title: Strong subadditivity of topological entropy on the torus: R\'enyi order and non-Abelian structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.20078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify canonical R\'enyi strong subadditivity on an unpunctured torus for finite unitary modular categories. For all pure logical states and admissible region pairs, validity at 0<alpha<1 is equivalent to Abelianity; at alpha=1 it is universal. Each finite non-Abelian group G has a pure untwisted D(G) fixed-point ground state with an order-two violation under ordinary edge partial traces. A specified local-filter D(S_3) family changes reduced spectra; its fixed-cut deficit tends to the negative fixed-point value over a small size-independent interval in a controlled joint limit.
item.dc:creator: Yi Liang

item.title: Anticommuting Displacement Operators, Exact Pauli Algebras,and the Singlet State from the Oscillator Vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.23264v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an explicit construction of a pair of anticommuting Weyl displacement operators for a harmonic oscillator and use bounded functional calculus to obtain exact dichotomic representatives of the Pauli algebra. Two independent oscillators provide commuting Pauli algebras for Alice and Bob. The standard singlet-sector projector, written entirely in terms of these bounded oscillator observables, is then applied to the two-oscillator vacuum. We show explicitly that the projected vacuum has nonzero norm, so its normalization is well defined, has the exact singlet correlations, and reaches the Tsirelson value $2\sqrt2$ for the usual Bell--CHSH settings. We also clarify that the construction generally realizes a singlet sector with multiplicity, rather than selecting a unique vector in the full oscillator Hilbert space, and we compare the construction with the older pseudospin approach to continuous-variable Bell tests.
item.dc:creator: S. P. Sorella

item.title: PPT-assisted capacities of bosonic Gaussian channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.26783v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the exact quantum communication and entanglement-distribution capacities of three fundamental bosonic channels, namely thermal loss, thermal amplification and additive Gaussian noise, assisted by operations that completely preserve positive partial transpose (PPT). These operations are more powerful than local operations and classical communication (LOCC), but cannot generate distillable entanglement on their own. For thermal loss, the unconstrained capacity coincides with the Pirandola-Laurenza-Ottaviani-Banchi (PLOB) bound throughout the non-entanglement-breaking regime. The corresponding upper bounds are also attained for thermal amplification and additive noise. We extend these results to energy-constrained communication, establishing exact capacities for all three channels at every prescribed mean input energy. Our results solve a class of bosonic capacity problems under PPT assistance and establish exact benchmarks for determining whether the same communication rates can be achieved via LOCC alone.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Barber, Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2610.26833v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Machine learning is widely regarded as a promising application in which quantum computing could offer a computational advantage. However, general quantum machine learning models with provable guarantees on performance, trainability, and efficient inference remain limited. In this work, we introduce quantum Hamiltonian embeddings, a supervised learning framework in which a classical training dataset is encoded into a single effective, parameterized Hamiltonian. Training optimizes the parameters of this data-dependent Hamiltonian, whose approximate ground state defines the classification rule. Once the ground state has been approximated using a quantum algorithm, inference can be performed either classically using a classical representation of the learned state, or with a quantum representation of the state. We establish efficient methods for gradient estimation and prove favorable generalization guarantees. Furthermore, under standard cryptographic assumptions, we show that Hamiltonian embeddings can realize hypothesis functions beyond the reach of efficient classical algorithms. We then demonstrate the framework at scale on IBM Heron processors using a standard benchmark dataset. Together, these results establish Hamiltonian embeddings as a new framework for quantum machine learning, combining theoretical guarantees with a path for experimental investigations at scale on quantum hardware.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Molteni, Minjun Jeon, Paolo Braccia, Abhinav Deshpande, Vedran Dunjko, Liang Jiang, Su-un Lee, Swarnadeep Majumder, Javier Robledo Moreno, Parthasarathy Suryanarayanan, Kunal Sharma

item.title: Collision-aware Bayesian mitigation of photon loss in linear optical quantum circuits
item.description: arXiv:2610.27529v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Photon loss is the dominant noise source in linear optical quantum circuits. Each lost photon turns an ideal n-photon outcome into a pattern with fewer photons, so the detector counts no longer follow the ideal output distribution, and the lossless events that do follow it become exponentially rare as the photon number grows. Discarding the lossy events (postselection) therefore wastes most of the data at realistic loss rates, and the ideal distribution has to be inferred from the lossy counts themselves. Recycling-based mitigation (Mills & Mezher, Quantum 2026; Quandela's photon_recycling) reweights lossy samples to recover lossless probabilities, but its estimators are biased and restricted to the no-collision sector, where each output mode holds at most one photon. We instead treat the raw counts as Multinomial observations under per-photon binomial loss and infer the ideal output distribution and the loss rate jointly from a Bayesian posterior, which extends naturally to outputs with collisions. On data from the independent Perceval simulator at the scale of prior work (n=4 photons in m=20 and m=10 modes), the posterior has lower KL divergence than both recycling and postselection at every tested loss rate in the no-collision benchmark. In the collision regime it recovers the loss rate and the collision-pattern probabilities, which recycling cannot estimate, and stays below recycling at every loss rate and below postselection except at low loss, where the two are comparable. Its advantage over recycling grows with the sample count, and it supplies credible intervals that the baselines lack.
item.dc:creator: Seungwoo Kim, Hyunho Cha, Jungwoo Lee, Seunghyun Ahn, Donguk Nam

item.title: Relativistic Strong Quantum Mpemba Effect
item.description: arXiv:2610.28017v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Unruh effect links acceleration to thermalization, providing a relativistic setting for anomalous quantum relaxation. We demonstrate a {\it relativistic} strong quantum Mpemba effect in the Unruh thermalization of a two-level detector coupled to a massless scalar field. For a fixed pair of isospectral initial states, relaxation curves that never cross in inertial motion exhibit a Mpemba crossing above a threshold acceleration. At a higher, precisely tuned acceleration, the initially farther state has zero overlap with the slowest decay mode and relaxes with a faster asymptotic exponential rate. We identify how competition between transition and dephasing channels governs the relaxation spectrum, where sufficiently strong longitudinal coupling enables acceleration to switch the relaxation bottleneck between population and coherence modes. We derive the spectral-switching condition and construct isospectral preparation protocols that eliminate slow-mode contributions within their physical domains. Our results establish acceleration as a control parameter for anomalous quantum relaxation, connecting relativistic quantum dynamics with nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
item.dc:creator: Zhilong Liu, Zehua Tian, Hui Jing, Jieci Wang

item.title: Bias-Preserving Entanglement of Kerr-Cat Qubits with an ATS Coupler
item.description: arXiv:2610.28749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kerr-cat qubits offer a hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computing by suppressing bit-flip errors exponentially, while phase-flip errors increase only linearly with the mean photon number. To maintain this protection, entangling operations must be bias-preserving, ensuring that phase-flip errors occurring during the gate do not propagate into bit-flip errors. In this paper, we propose an asymmetrically threaded SQUID (ATS) parametric coupler to implement high-fidelity, bias-preserving entangling gates between Kerr-cat qubits. By engineering a photon-number asymmetry between the control and target modes, we enable fast gate operations that suppress non-adiabatic leakage without complex pulse shaping. Through numerical simulations of the full circuit Hamiltonian, we demonstrate a bias-preserving CX gate achieving 99.69% fidelity in the absence of photon loss for a gate duration of 50 ns. Under a single-photon loss rate of 100 kHz, our protocol yields a noise bias of 9922, exceeding the noise bias of a naive non-bias-preserving CX implementation by approximately a factor of 570. These results support the ATS coupler as a valuable building block for concatenated cat-qubit architectures.
item.dc:creator: Kerem Yurtseven, Shantanu R. Jha, Apoorva Limaye, Risav Pokhrel, Maral Mahmoudi Kamelabad, Muhammad Waqar Amin

item.title: Photon Correlations Control Quantum Fisher Information in Coherent Multidimensional Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2610.29422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coherent multidimensional spectroscopy probes interactions and dynamics of molecular systems through nonlinear optical signals. Quantum light excitation has been explored as a means of controlling these signals, raising the question of how excitation-light correlations affect the precision of molecular parameter estimation from the emitted signal. In this work, we show that photon-number correlations and two-photon coherence play distinct roles in encoding molecular information in the emitted rephasing signal. In the weak-emission regime and within the single Schmidt pair approximation, we derive a normally ordered information law in which the joint photon-number moment and the squared magnitude of the two-photon coherence weight the amplitude and phase sensitivities of the molecular response, respectively. For matched temporal modes and mean photon numbers in each input mode, two-mode squeezed vacuum enhances both weights relative to coherent excitation, whereas independent displaced squeezing preserves the amplitude weight but reduces the phase weight. The background population and its parameter dependence also affect the total quantum Fisher information, which therefore cannot be inferred from the coherent mean-field signal alone. We derive a leading-order bound on its enhancement over coherent excitation when the background population is nonnegative and common to the compared sources. These findings provide criteria for selecting excitation sources according to how the target molecular parameter affects the amplitude and phase of the response.
item.dc:creator: Chenghong Huang, Yuta Fujihashi, Akihito Ishizaki

item.title: Encoding a bosonic mode into qubits for simulating boson-matter interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.29762v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explore the space-time cost of encoding of a bosonic mode into a set of qubits via various encodings, and their resilience to noise. In particular, we compare the performance of the unary Fock state encoding, an unexplored encoding of Fock states into Dicke states (``Dicke'' encoding), and the binary quadrature encoding. We do so by considering a displacement as well as a simulation of a Dicke model, coupling a bosonic mode to a set of atoms represented as qubits. Using classical simulations, we assess the accuracy and optimized space-time costs in terms of number of qubits, circuit depth and CNOT count of a quantum simulation of the time dynamics using these encodings. Although our study is far from comprehensive, we find that the binary quadrature encoding is overall most favorable in terms of being very space-efficient and relatively time-efficient due to the use of the quantum Fourier transform. Our novel Dicke encoding leads to very shallow circuits, but pays in terms of using many more qubits. We probe the use of an H2-2 Quantinuum trapped-ion qubit device (56 qubits) for displacement and Dicke model simulation in the low boson-number regime, where we find that noise leads to visible deviations from ideal circuit dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Maarten Stroeks, Jelena Mackeprang, Yaroslav Herasymenko, Barbara Terhal

item.title: Naive Quantum Gravity
item.description: arXiv:1502.02058v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A possible alternative route to a quantum theory of gravity is described. The usual path quantises the gravitational field in order to introduce the statistical structure characteristic of quantum mechanics. The procedure followed here instead is to remove the probabilistic element of quantum theory by using the less-common technique of introducing final boundary conditions as well as initial on the source. The relevant quantum formalism then becomes compatible with the non-statistical nature of general relativity and a viable theory can be constructed without difficulty. The view taken here is that the lack of both experimental guidance and theoretical consensus lends justification to considering such less mainstream ideas.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Quantum Studies: Mathematics and Foundations, Vol. 13, Article 38 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Roderick Sutherland

item.title: Thermodynamic compatibility, holographic property and wave-function representation of generalized weakly nonlocal self-gravitating non-relativistic fluids
item.description: arXiv:2504.07296v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Two pillars of physics---gravity and quantum mechanics---are usually formulated in entirely separate languages. Surprisingly, both can be expressed in the language of a fluid: a self-gravitating fluid for Newtonian gravity, and a quantum-pressure-carrying fluid for the Schr\"odinger equation. In this work we show that this resemblance can be understood within a common framework based on how the Second Law of Thermodynamics constrains the class of non-dissipative continua considered here. Using a transparent thermodynamic procedure, we derive the most general fluid model within a chosen constitutive state space involving density, velocity, energy, an internal scalar field, and their spatial gradients. The framework recovers, as special cases, the Euler equations, a restricted family of Korteweg fluids (including the hydrodynamic form of the Schr\"odinger and Gross--Pitaevskii equations), Newtonian self-gravitating fluids, and the Schr\"odinger--Newton system. We identify the conditions under which perfect fluids exhibit \emph{classical holography}: the pressure-tensor divergence can then be represented by the gradient of a scalar potential. Classical holography yields a vorticity transport law that preserves sufficiently regular, initially irrotational flows and, under additional assumptions, enables a single complex-valued Schr\"odinger-like representation. While gravitational and quantum-hydrodynamic theories were investigated separately in our previous works, the present study develops a substantially more general scalar-internal-variable construction, refines its perfect-fluid analysis, and systematically embeds the earlier models within a unified framework. The framework also identifies a thermodynamically admissible density--gravity coupling that connects classical and quantum self-gravitating fluids, although its stability, and observational consequences remain to be explored.
item.dc:creator: M\'aty\'as Sz\"ucs, P\'eter V\'an

item.title: Subspace-Protected Topological Phases and Bulk-Boundary Correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2508.20908v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While tremendous research has revealed that symmetry enriches topological phases of matter, more general principles that protect topological phases have yet to be explored. In this Letter, we elucidate the roles of subspaces in free-fermionic topological phases. A subspace property for Hamiltonians enables us to define new topological invariants. It results in peculiar topological boundary phenomena, i.e., the emergence of an unpaired zero mode or zero-winding skin modes, characterizing subspace-protected topological phases. We establish and demonstrate the bulk-boundary correspondence in subspace-protected topological phases. We further discuss the interplay of the subspace property and internal symmetries. Toward application, we also propose possible platforms possessing the subspace property.
item.dc:creator: Kenji Shimomura, Ryo Takami, Daichi Nakamura, Masatoshi Sato

item.title: Landscape of scattering universality with general dispersion relations
item.description: arXiv:2509.01782v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Universality in physics describes how disparate systems can exhibit identical low-energy behavior. Here, we reveal a rich landscape of new universal scattering phenomena governed by the interplay between an interaction and a system's density of states. We investigate one-dimensional scattering with dispersion relations $\epsilon(k)=|k|^m$ and $\epsilon(k)=\operatorname{sgn}(k)|k|^m$ for any real $m>1$. For emitter scattering and separable potentials, including contact potentials, we classify the zero-energy $S$-matrix limits. These universal $S$-matrix fixed points depend solely on the dispersion exponent $m$ and a finite set of integers characterizing the low-momentum interaction structure. This classification extends far beyond the standard quadratic-dispersion case ($m=2$). We further derive a generalized Levinson's theorem relating the total winding of the $S$-matrix determinant to the number of bound states. Finally, for contact potentials and analytic monomial dispersions, we analyze the leading low-energy expansion of the scattering phase near these fixed points and extract the corresponding Wigner-delay scaling. Our findings are directly relevant to synthetic quantum systems, where engineered dispersion relations in atomic arrays and photonic crystals offer a platform to explore these universal behaviors.
item.dc:creator: Yidan Wang, Xuesen Na, Michael J. Gullans, Susanne Yelin, Alexey V. Gorshkov

item.title: Web of Non-invertible Dualities for (2+1) Dimensional Models with Subsystem Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2511.18969v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend non-invertible duality concepts from one-dimensional systems to two spatial dimensions by constructing a web of non-invertible dualities for lattice models with subsystem symmetries. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ subsystem symmetry on the square lattice, we build two complementary dualities: a map that sends spontaneous subsystem symmetry-broken (SSSB) phases to the trivial phase (the analogue of the Kramers-Wannier (KW) duality in 1+1D), and a generalized subsystem Kennedy-Tasaki (KT) transformation that maps SSSB phases to subsystem symmetry-protected topological (SSPT) phases while leaving the trivial phase invariant. These dualities are boundary-sensitive. On open lattices, both subsystem KW and KT transformations act as unitary, invertible operators. In particular, the KT map not only matches the bulk Hamiltonians of the dual phases but also carries the spontaneous ground-state degeneracy of the SSSB phase onto the protected boundary degeneracy of the SSPT phase. On closed manifolds, however, both maps become intrinsically non-unitary and non-invertible when restricted to the original Hilbert space. We demonstrate this non-invertibility via ground-state degeneracy matching (in two copies of the Xu-Moore/Ising-plaquette model), analysis of symmetry-twist sectors mapping, and the fusion algebra of the duality operator. Enlarging the Hilbert space to include twisted sectors allows the subsystem KW map to be formulated as a projective unitary preserving quantum transition probabilities, consistent with generalized Wigner-theorem-based constructions. We also show that the KT map faithfully transmits the algebraic content of bulk and edge invariants diagnosing strong SSPT order: although strictly local SSPT repair operators map to highly nonlocal objects in the dual SSSB phase, the essential commutation algebra and the bulk-edge correspondence remain intact.
item.dc:creator: Avijit Maity, Vikram Tripathi, Andriy H. Nevidomskyy

item.title: Explicit complex time integrators for stiff problems
item.description: arXiv:2601.07730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Most numerical methods for time integration use real-valued time steps. Complex time steps, however, can provide an additional degree of freedom, as we can select the magnitude of the time step in both the real and imaginary directions. We show that specific paths in the complex time plane lead to expanded stability regions, providing clear computational advantages for complex-valued systems. In particular, we highlight the Schr\"odinger equation, for which complex time integrators can be uniquely optimal. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these benefits extend to certain classes of real-valued stiff systems by coupling complex time steps with the Projective Integration method.
item.dc:creator: Jithin D. George, Julian Koellermeier, Samuel Y. Jung, Niall M. Mangan

item.title: Rabi oscillations induced by nonresonant gyrating drive
item.description: arXiv:2602.11979v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coherent control of two-level quantum systems is typically achieved using resonant driving fields, forming the basis for qubit operations. Here, we report a mechanism for inducing complete Rabi oscillations in monochromatically driven two-level quantum systems, when the drive frequency is much larger than the Larmor frequency of the qubit. This effect$\unicode{x2015}$Rabi oscillations induced by nonresonant gyrating drive (RING)$\unicode{x2015}$requires a gyrating control field, i.e., an elliptic drive trajectory that encloses a nonzero area per cycle. We illustrate the effect with numerical simulations, and provide an analytical understanding via a simple effective Hamiltonian obtained from Floquet theory and perturbation theory. We show that RING enables coherent oscillations without relying on resonant energy exchange, allows for high-pass noise filtering, provides access to non-Abelian phases in finite magnetic fields. We detail a realization in electrically driven spin-orbit qubits and argue that the RING mechanism enables amplification of the Rabi frequency using the same gate voltage amplitudes at higher drive frequencies. Our results broaden the landscape of quantum control techniques, by highlighting a pathway to achieving coherent oscillations under off-resonant driving conditions.
item.dc:creator: Baksa Kolok, Andr\'as P\'alyi

item.title: Experimental probe of quantum coherence in top-quark pair production at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2602.21069v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate quantum coherence in the spin degrees of freedom of top--antitop pairs produced at the LHC using the $l_1$-norm of coherence in the helicity basis. Combining Standard Model predictions with the spin density matrix reconstructed from the CMS measurement of top-quark spin correlation coefficients, we study the dependence of coherence on the invariant mass $M_{t\bar t}$ and production angle. To quantify the experimental precision of the extracted coherence, we propagate the measured uncertainties and covariance matrix of the spin-correlation coefficients through a Monte Carlo procedure. We find a non-monotonic kinematic dependence: coherence is large near the production threshold, is reduced in the intermediate-mass region, and increases again in boosted central events. The theoretical predictions are in good agreement with the CMS determinations in all three kinematic regions. Moreover, the experimentally reconstructed coherence is nonzero with a significance exceeding $5\sigma$ in each region. In particular, in the intermediate-mass region, $400<M_{t\bar t}<600~\mathrm{GeV}$, we obtain $C_{l_1}=0.597\pm0.037$. This result is especially noteworthy because previous analyses of the same reconstructed top-quark spin density matrix found concurrence and negativity, both entanglement measures, to be consistent with zero, $0.00\pm0.02$, in this kinematic region. The persistence of sizable coherence where entanglement is not experimentally certified demonstrates that coherence provides complementary information on the off-diagonal helicity-interference structure of the top-quark spin density matrix. Our results establish quantum coherence as an experimentally accessible and statistically robust observable for probing the quantum structure of top-quark pair production at the LHC.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Haddadi, Majid Azizi, Artur Czerwinski, Hamid Arian Zad

item.title: AlphaCNOT: Learning CNOT Minimization with Model-Based Planning
item.description: arXiv:2604.13812v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum circuit optimization is a central task in quantum computing, as current NISQ devices suffer from error propagation that often scales with the number of operations. Among quantum operations, the CNOT gate is of fundamental importance, being the only two-qubit gate in the universal Clifford+T set. Minimizing CNOT gates is therefore particularly important, as these gates exhibit higher error rates and they typically introduce additional routing overhead due to hardware constraints. The problem of CNOT gate minimization has been addressed by heuristic algorithms such as the well-known Patel-Markov-Hayes (PMH) for linear reversible synthesis (i.e., CNOT minimization with no topological constraints), and more recently by Reinforcement Learning (RL) based strategies in the more complex case of topology-aware synthesis, where each CNOT can act on a subset of qubit pairs. We introduce AlphaCNOT, an RL framework based on Monte Carlo Tree Search that effectively addresses the CNOT minimization problem by modeling it as a planning problem. In contrast to other RL-based solutions, our method is model-based, i.e., it can leverage lookahead search to evaluate future trajectories, thus finding more efficient sequences of CNOTs. Our method achieves a reduction of up to 24.62% in CNOT count compared with the PMH baseline on linear reversible synthesis, and a consistent gate count reduction on different topologies with up to 8 qubits, also with respect to state-of-the-art RL-based solutions. Our results suggest the combination of RL with search-based strategies can be applied to different circuit optimization tasks, thus fostering the transition toward the "quantum utility" era.
item.dc:creator: Jacopo Cossio, Daniele Lizzio Bosco, Riccardo Romanello, Giuseppe Serra, Carla Piazza

item.title: Unveiling Topological Fusion in Quantum Hall Systems from Microscopic Principles
item.description: arXiv:2604.16525v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Establishing the fusion rules of anyonic quasiparticles in fractional quantum Hall fluids is essential for understanding their underlying topological order. Building on the conjecture that key topological properties are encoded in the ''DNA'' of candidate many-body wave functions - that is, the pattern of dominant orbital occupations restricted to a finite number of lowest Landau levels - we propose a combinatorial framework that derives these fusion rules directly from microscopic data. By extending Schrieffer's counting argument and introducing classes of topological excitations, our framework provides a unified route to the fusion rules for both Abelian and non-Abelian excitations. This approach elucidates the emergence of topological features from first principles in both fermionic and bosonic systems. In particular, we unveil the previously unknown fusion rules of the Hafnian fluid.
item.dc:creator: Arkadiusz Bochniak, Shinsei Ryu, J\"urgen Fuchs, Gerardo Ortiz

item.title: Fidelity-Guaranteed Entanglement Routing with Distributed Purification Planning
item.description: arXiv:2605.00246v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many quantum-network applications require end-to-end Bell pairs whose fidelity exceeds a request-specific threshold, but existing entanglement routing algorithms either optimize only throughput without regard for fidelity or enforce fidelity guarantees using centralized controllers with global link-state knowledge. We present Q-GUARD, an online entanglement routing algorithm that enforces per-request fidelity thresholds within a distributed protocol model in which nodes exchange link-state information only with their $k$-hop neighbors. After link outcomes are realized in each slot, Q-GUARD builds per-link purification cost tables from realized Bell pairs, allocates per-hop fidelity targets using a Werner-state equal-split rule, and selects between candidate path segments using a segment-local expected-goodput (EXG) metric that jointly accounts for swap success, purification overhead, and resource availability. We also introduce Q-GUARD-WS, an extension that exploits per-link hardware quality estimates to allocate purification effort non-uniformly across hops. On synthetic 100-node topologies with heterogeneous link fidelity and stochastic BBPSSW purification, Q-GUARD raises the qualified success rate from under 20\% to over 85\% on 4-hop paths and nearly doubles the qualified service radius in Euclidean distance relative to throughput-only and naive-purification baselines, while Q-GUARD-WS provides additional throughput gains under high hardware heterogeneity.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Gatti, Anoosha Fayyaz, Prashant Krishnamurthy, Kaushik P. Seshadreesan, Amy Babay

item.title: The Kubo-Thermalization Correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2605.06666v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum thermalization describes how interacting quantum systems relax toward thermal equilibrium, a central problem in modern physics. Yet most experimental information on many-body systems comes from short-time transition spectroscopy, typically interpreted within Kubo's linear-response framework. These perspectives-long-time equilibration versus short-time response-seem fundamentally disconnected. Here we establish an exact link between them: the \emph{Kubo-Thermalization correspondence}, which connects long-time thermalized magnetization under weak driving to short-time linear-response spectra for a spin coupled to a thermal bath. The correspondence holds even when the steady state differs substantially from the initial state and when each regime is individually difficult to describe theoretically. We experimentally confirm the correspondence using effective spin-$1/2$ impurities realized with ultracold fermions in two internal states coupled to a Fermi sea. Our results provide a rare exact statement about quantum thermalization and offer a novel route to infer thermalization dynamics from equilibrium response measurements in strongly interacting quantum systems, independent of microscopic details of the system--bath coupling.
item.dc:creator: Songtao Huang, Xingyu Li, Jianyi Chen, Alan Tsidilkovski, Gabriel G. T. Assump\c{c}\~ao, Pengfei Zhang, Hui Zhai, Nir Navon

item.title: Twirled Perfect Tensor Networks: Computationally covariant holographic tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2605.23670v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define a novel class of tensor networks motivated by the Python's Lunch Conjecture (PLC) in local tensor network models of the black hole interior. We start from the observation that, for extended black brane states with short-range correlations, the PLC predicts a complexity that is smaller than the upper bound for generic short-range correlated states. We argue that the PLC makes implicit assumptions about the fine structure of the relevant tensor networks modeling gravity that render them non-generic. We demonstrate this explicitly in random tensor network models of the python's lunch, where the exponential complexity is not generally controlled by the PLC exponent.
